Allah, glorified is He, commanded him (the Prophet ﷺ) to inform them, when their demands upon him and their obstinate insistence on the sending down of signs that would compel them to faith had multiplied, that he did not have the treasuries of Allah, so as to bring them the signs they had proposed. What is meant by "the treasuries of Allah" is the treasuries of His power, which encompass everything. He is also to tell them that he does not know the unseen, so as to inform them of it and make them aware of what will happen in the future of time. And he is to say to them, "I do not tell you that I am an angel, so that you may impose upon me acts that exceed custom and that no human can bear." There is nothing in this that indicates the angels are superior to the prophets. A group of the people of knowledge have occupied themselves with this question of superiority, though no religious or worldly benefit follows from it.

Rather, discussion of such a matter is among the preoccupations with what does not concern a person, and part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him. ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾: that is, I follow only what Allah reveals to me. Those who deny that the prophets exercised independent reasoning (ijtihad, the scholarly effort to derive rulings) have held to this, acting on what the restrictive form (al-qasr, the restriction of a predicate to a subject) in this verse conveys. The issue is codified in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh), and the evidence for it is well known. It is authentically related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "I have been given the Qur'an and the like of it with it."

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ This interrogative is for denial. What is meant is that the one who is astray and the one who is guided are not equal, or the Muslim and the disbelievers, or the one who follows what has been revealed to him and the one who does not follow it. The statement is an analogy. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ so that you may know the inequality between the two, for it is clear and is not obscured to one who has the least intelligence and the slightest reflection. (p-٤٢١)

His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾. Al-indhar (warning) means informing.

The pronoun in "thereby" refers to what is revealed. It was said that it refers to Allah, and it was said that it refers to the Last Day.

He specified those who fear being gathered because warning affects them on account of the fear that has descended upon them, unlike one of the groups of disbelief who does not fear the gathering, due to his denial of it and his rejection of it, for such warning does not affect him.

It was said: the meaning of "fear" here is "know" and "be certain" that they will be gathered, so it includes every believer in resurrection from among the Muslims, the protected people (ahl al-dhimma, non-Muslim subjects under Muslim protection), and some of the polytheists. It was also said: the meaning of fear is its literal sense, and the meaning is that he warns with it those in whom fear of the gathering becomes evident upon hearing the Prophet (ﷺ) remind them, even if he was not affirming it originally, but he fears that what the Prophet (ﷺ) reported may be true. For whoever is like this, admonition is most effective with him and reminder most beneficial to him.

His saying: ﴿They have besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): that is, warn with it those who fear the gathering, while they have no protector who supports them, no helper who aids them, and no intercessor who intercedes for them apart from Allah. In this there is a refutation of those disbelievers who acknowledged the gathering and claimed that their forefathers would intercede for them, these being the People of the Book, or that their idols would intercede for them, these being the polytheists.

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face﴾. Al-du'a' (supplication) here means worship in general. It was said: it means maintaining the congregational prayer. It was said: it means remembrance and recitation of the Qur'an. It was said: what is meant is supplication to Allah for bringing benefit and averting harm.

It was said: the mention of morning and evening means constancy and continuity in this. It was also said that it is on its apparent meaning. And ﴿seeking His face﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause.

The meaning is that they are sincere in their worship, seeking by it nothing but the face of Allah, the Exalted: that is, they turn with it toward Him and not toward anything else.

His saying: ﴿Upon you is not any of their account, and upon them is not any of your account﴾. This is a parenthetical statement between the prohibition and its answer, containing the negation of what would motivate the driving away. That is: the account of those whom you wished to drive away, in compliance with one who asked you to do so, is upon themselves, and nothing of it is upon you; and your account is upon yourself, and nothing of it is upon them. So why would you drive them away? This is on the supposition of the truth of the description of those who described them with His saying: ﴿And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us﴾ [Hud: 27], and who slandered their religion and lineage in your presence. How much more so when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commended them for worship and sincerity. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and His saying: ﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for﴾ [al-Najm: 39], and His saying: ﴿Their account is only upon my Lord﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 113].

His saying: ﴿So you would drive them away﴾ is the answer to the negation in His saying: ﴿Upon you is not any of their account﴾, and it is part of the parenthetical statement. That is: if the matter is so, then turn to them, sit with them, and do not drive them away, out of regard for the right of one who is not in their condition in religion and merit. The "min" in ﴿min hisabihim min shay'in﴾ is partitive, and the second is for emphasis, and likewise in ﴿wa ma min hisabika 'alayhim min shay'in﴾.

His saying: ﴿So you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is the answer to the prohibition, namely ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾. That is: if you did that, you would be among the wrongdoers. He is far from committing that, and this is only by way of allusion, lest anyone else among the Muslims, other than the Prophet (ﷺ), do likewise, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your work would surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]. It was said that ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is conjoined to ﴿so you would drive them away﴾ by way of causation, but the first is preferable.

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them by means of others﴾. That is: like that great trial, We tried some people by means of others. Fitna (trial) here means testing: that is, We dealt with them as testers deal. The lam in ﴿liyaqulu﴾ ("that they might say") indicates result (lam al-'aqibah): that is, so that the first group might say, pointing to the second group, "Are these the ones whom Allah has favored among us?" That is, He honored them by guiding them to the truth rather than us.

Al-Nahhas said: This is among the difficult points, for it is asked: how were they tried so that they would say this statement, which, if it was in the manner of denial, is disbelief? He answered with two answers. The first: that this was said by them in the manner of a question, not in the manner of denial. The second: that when they were tested by this, its consequence was this statement from them, like His saying: ﴿So the household of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas: 8].

His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ This interrogative is for affirmation. The meaning is that the basis of entitlement to the blessings of Allah, glorified is He, is gratitude, and He is most knowing of those who are grateful to Him. So what is the matter with you that you object out of ignorance and deny the grace?

His saying: ﴿And when those come to you who believe in Our signs﴾: they are those whom Allah forbade him to drive away, and they are the oppressed among the believers, as its explanation will come. ﴿Say: Peace be upon you.﴾ Allah commanded him to say this statement to them, as a comforting of their hearts and an honoring of them.

Al-salam and al-salama have the same meaning, so the meaning of "salamun 'alaykum" is: may Allah keep you safe.

After the revelation of this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he saw them, would greet them first with peace. It was also said that this peace is from Allah: that is, convey to them peace from us.

His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾: that is, He made this obligatory as an obligation of grace and kindness. It was also said that He wrote this in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

It was said: this is among what Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to convey to those to whom He commanded him to convey the greeting, as good tidings of the vastness of Allah's forgiveness and the greatness of His mercy.

His saying: ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, and Nafi' read "annahu" with a fatha on the alif (anna), and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, this clause is a substitute (badal) for "mercy": that is, your Lord has prescribed for Himself that whoever of you does (and so on to the end).

On the second reading, this clause explains "mercy" by way of a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), and the position of "bi-jahalah" (in ignorance) is accusative as a circumstantial clause: that is, he did it while being ignorant.

It was said: the meaning is that he acted as the ignorant act, for whoever does what leads to harm in the outcome, while knowing or suspecting it, has acted as the people of ignorance and foolishness act, not as the people of wisdom and prudence act. It was also said: the meaning is that he did it while ignorant of the harm attached to it, and so the purpose of restricting it to ignorance is to indicate that the believer does not engage in what he knows leads to harm.

His saying: ﴿Then repents after it﴾: that is, after his action, and rectifies what he corrupted by disobedience, so he returns to the right and performs obedience. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim (p-٤٢٢) read "fa-annahu" with a fatha on the hamza, and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, "anna" and what follows it is the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, "so His command is that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." This is the choice of Sibawayh. Abu Hatim chose that the clause is in the nominative position as the subject, with an omitted predicate, as if it were said: "so for him is: 'indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.'" He said: because the subject is what follows the fa'.

As for the second reading, the clause is a resumptive sentence.

His saying: ﴿And thus We detail the signs﴾: that is, like that detailing We detail them. Tafsil (detailing) means clarification.

The meaning is that Allah has made clear to them what they need of the matters of religion and has explained to them the ruling for every group.

His saying: ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾.

The Kufans said: it is conjoined to an implied element: that is, "and thus We detail the signs, so that We may clarify to you and that it may become evident." Al-Nahhas said: this deletion is not needed.

It was also said that the entry of the waw is for conjunction according to meaning. "Li-tastabina" has been read with the second person (ta, feminine/upper) and with the third person (ya, lower). The address in the second person is to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, that you, O Muhammad, may make evident the way of the criminals. "Sabil" is in the accusative in the reading of Nafi'. As for the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs, with the nominative, the verb is attributed to "sabil." As for the third person, the verb is also attributed to "sabil," and this is the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Shu'ba with the nominative. When the way of the criminals becomes evident, the way of the believers has become evident as well.

A group of the people of knowledge have occupied themselves with this question of superiority, though no religious or worldly benefit follows from it.

His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾. Al-indhar (warning) means informing.

The pronoun in "thereby" refers to what is revealed. It was said that it refers to Allah, and it was said that it refers to the Last Day.

He specified those who fear being gathered because warning affects them on account of the fear that has descended upon them, unlike one of the groups of disbelief who does not fear the gathering, due to his denial of it and his rejection of it, for such warning does not affect him.

It was said: the meaning of "fear" here is "know" and "be certain" that they will be gathered, so it includes every believer in resurrection from among the Muslims, the protected people (ahl al-dhimma, non-Muslim subjects under Muslim protection), and some of the polytheists. It was also said: the meaning of fear is its literal sense, and the meaning is that he warns with it those in whom fear of the gathering becomes evident upon hearing the Prophet (ﷺ) remind them, even if he was not affirming it originally, but he fears that what the Prophet (ﷺ) reported may be true. For whoever is like this, admonition is most effective with him and reminder most beneficial to him.

His saying: ﴿They have besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): that is, warn with it those who fear the gathering, while they have no protector who supports them, no helper who aids them, and no intercessor who intercedes for them apart from Allah. In this there is a refutation of those disbelievers who acknowledged the gathering and claimed that their forefathers would intercede for them, these being the People of the Book, or that their idols would intercede for them, these being the polytheists.

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face﴾. Al-du'a' (supplication) here means worship in general. It was said: it means maintaining the congregational prayer. It was said: it means remembrance and recitation of the Qur'an. It was said: what is meant is supplication to Allah for bringing benefit and averting harm.

It was said: the mention of morning and evening means constancy and continuity in this. It was also said that it is on its apparent meaning. And ﴿seeking His face﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause.

The meaning is that they are sincere in their worship, seeking by it nothing but the face of Allah, the Exalted: that is, they turn with it toward Him and not toward anything else.

His saying: ﴿Upon you is not any of their account, and upon them is not any of your account﴾. This is a parenthetical statement between the prohibition and its answer, containing the negation of what would motivate the driving away. That is: the account of those whom you wished to drive away, in compliance with one who asked you to do so, is upon themselves, and nothing of it is upon you; and your account is upon yourself, and nothing of it is upon them. So why would you drive them away? This is on the supposition of the truth of the description of those who described them with His saying: ﴿And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us﴾ [Hud: 27], and who slandered their religion and lineage in your presence. How much more so when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commended them for worship and sincerity. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and His saying: ﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for﴾ [al-Najm: 39], and His saying: ﴿Their account is only upon my Lord﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 113].

His saying: ﴿So you would drive them away﴾ is the answer to the negation in His saying: ﴿Upon you is not any of their account﴾, and it is part of the parenthetical statement. That is: if the matter is so, then turn to them, sit with them, and do not drive them away, out of regard for the right of one who is not in their condition in religion and merit. The "min" in ﴿min hisabihim min shay'in﴾ is partitive, and the second is for emphasis, and likewise in ﴿wa ma min hisabika 'alayhim min shay'in﴾.

His saying: ﴿So you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is the answer to the prohibition, namely ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾. That is: if you did that, you would be among the wrongdoers. He is far from committing that, and this is only by way of allusion, lest anyone else among the Muslims, other than the Prophet (ﷺ), do likewise, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your work would surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]. It was said that ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is conjoined to ﴿so you would drive them away﴾ by way of causation, but the first is preferable.

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them by means of others﴾. That is: like that great trial, We tried some people by means of others. Fitna (trial) here means testing: that is, We dealt with them as testers deal. The lam in ﴿liyaqulu﴾ ("that they might say") indicates result (lam al-'aqibah): that is, so that the first group might say, pointing to the second group, "Are these the ones whom Allah has favored among us?" That is, He honored them by guiding them to the truth rather than us.

Al-Nahhas said: This is among the difficult points, for it is asked: how were they tried so that they would say this statement, which, if it was in the manner of denial, is disbelief? He answered with two answers. The first: that this was said by them in the manner of a question, not in the manner of denial. The second: that when they were tested by this, its consequence was this statement from them, like His saying: ﴿So the household of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas: 8].

His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ This interrogative is for affirmation. The meaning is that the basis of entitlement to the blessings of Allah, glorified is He, is gratitude, and He is most knowing of those who are grateful to Him. So what is the matter with you that you object out of ignorance and deny the grace?

His saying: ﴿And when those come to you who believe in Our signs﴾: they are those whom Allah forbade him to drive away, and they are the oppressed among the believers, as its explanation will come. ﴿Say: Peace be upon you.﴾ Allah commanded him to say this statement to them, as a comforting of their hearts and an honoring of them.

Al-salam and al-salama have the same meaning, so the meaning of "salamun 'alaykum" is: may Allah keep you safe.

After the revelation of this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he saw them, would greet them first with peace. It was also said that this peace is from Allah: that is, convey to them peace from us.

His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾: that is, He made this obligatory as an obligation of grace and kindness. It was also said that He wrote this in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

It was said: this is among what Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to convey to those to whom He commanded him to convey the greeting, as good tidings of the vastness of Allah's forgiveness and the greatness of His mercy.

His saying: ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, and Nafi' read "annahu" with a fatha on the alif (anna), and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, this clause is a substitute (badal) for "mercy": that is, your Lord has prescribed for Himself that whoever of you does (and so on to the end).

On the second reading, this clause explains "mercy" by way of a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), and the position of "bi-jahalah" (in ignorance) is accusative as a circumstantial clause: that is, he did it while being ignorant.

It was said: the meaning is that he acted as the ignorant act, for whoever does what leads to harm in the outcome, while knowing or suspecting it, has acted as the people of ignorance and foolishness act, not as the people of wisdom and prudence act. It was also said: the meaning is that he did it while ignorant of the harm attached to it, and so the purpose of restricting it to ignorance is to indicate that the believer does not engage in what he knows leads to harm.

His saying: ﴿Then repents after it﴾: that is, after his action, and rectifies what he corrupted by disobedience, so he returns to the right and performs obedience. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim (p-٤٢٢) read "fa-annahu" with a fatha on the hamza, and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, "anna" and what follows it is the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, "so His command is that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." This is the choice of Sibawayh. Abu Hatim chose that the clause is in the nominative position as the subject, with an omitted predicate, as if it were said: "so for him is: 'indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.'" He said: because the subject is what follows the fa'.

As for the second reading, the clause is a resumptive sentence.

His saying: ﴿And thus We detail the signs﴾: that is, like that detailing We detail them. Tafsil (detailing) means clarification.

The meaning is that Allah has made clear to them what they need of the matters of religion and has explained to them the ruling for every group.

His saying: ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾.

The Kufans said: it is conjoined to an implied element: that is, "and thus We detail the signs, so that We may clarify to you and that it may become evident." Al-Nahhas said: this deletion is not needed.

It was also said that the entry of the waw is for conjunction according to meaning. "Li-tastabina" has been read with the second person (ta, feminine/upper) and with the third person (ya, lower). The address in the second person is to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, that you, O Muhammad, may make evident the way of the criminals. "Sabil" is in the accusative in the reading of Nafi'. As for the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs, with the nominative, the verb is attributed to "sabil." As for the third person, the verb is also attributed to "sabil," and this is the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Shu'ba with the nominative. When the way of the criminals becomes evident, the way of the believers has become evident as well.

This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and His saying: ﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for﴾ [al-Najm: 39], and His saying: ﴿Their account is only upon my Lord﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 113].

His saying: ﴿So you would drive them away﴾ is the answer to the negation in His saying: ﴿Upon you is not any of their account﴾, and it is part of the parenthetical statement. That is: if the matter is so, then turn to them, sit with them, and do not drive them away, out of regard for the right of one who is not in their condition in religion and merit. The "min" in ﴿min hisabihim min shay'in﴾ is partitive, and the second is for emphasis, and likewise in ﴿wa ma min hisabika 'alayhim min shay'in﴾.

His saying: ﴿So you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is the answer to the prohibition, namely ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾. That is: if you did that, you would be among the wrongdoers. He is far from committing that, and this is only by way of allusion, lest anyone else among the Muslims, other than the Prophet (ﷺ), do likewise, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your work would surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]. It was said that ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is conjoined to ﴿so you would drive them away﴾ by way of causation, but the first is preferable.

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them by means of others﴾. That is: like that great trial, We tried some people by means of others. Fitna (trial) here means testing: that is, We dealt with them as testers deal. The lam in ﴿liyaqulu﴾ ("that they might say") indicates result (lam al-'aqibah): that is, so that the first group might say, pointing to the second group, "Are these the ones whom Allah has favored among us?" That is, He honored them by guiding them to the truth rather than us.

Al-Nahhas said: This is among the difficult points, for it is asked: how were they tried so that they would say this statement, which, if it was in the manner of denial, is disbelief? He answered with two answers. The first: that this was said by them in the manner of a question, not in the manner of denial. The second: that when they were tested by this, its consequence was this statement from them, like His saying: ﴿So the household of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas: 8].

His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ This interrogative is for affirmation. The meaning is that the basis of entitlement to the blessings of Allah, glorified is He, is gratitude, and He is most knowing of those who are grateful to Him. So what is the matter with you that you object out of ignorance and deny the grace?

His saying: ﴿And when those come to you who believe in Our signs﴾: they are those whom Allah forbade him to drive away, and they are the oppressed among the believers, as its explanation will come. ﴿Say: Peace be upon you.﴾ Allah commanded him to say this statement to them, as a comforting of their hearts and an honoring of them.

Al-salam and al-salama have the same meaning, so the meaning of "salamun 'alaykum" is: may Allah keep you safe.

After the revelation of this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he saw them, would greet them first with peace. It was also said that this peace is from Allah: that is, convey to them peace from us.

His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾: that is, He made this obligatory as an obligation of grace and kindness. It was also said that He wrote this in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

It was said: this is among what Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to convey to those to whom He commanded him to convey the greeting, as good tidings of the vastness of Allah's forgiveness and the greatness of His mercy.

His saying: ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, and Nafi' read "annahu" with a fatha on the alif (anna), and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, this clause is a substitute (badal) for "mercy": that is, your Lord has prescribed for Himself that whoever of you does (and so on to the end).

On the second reading, this clause explains "mercy" by way of a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), and the position of "bi-jahalah" (in ignorance) is accusative as a circumstantial clause: that is, he did it while being ignorant.

It was said: the meaning is that he acted as the ignorant act, for whoever does what leads to harm in the outcome, while knowing or suspecting it, has acted as the people of ignorance and foolishness act, not as the people of wisdom and prudence act. It was also said: the meaning is that he did it while ignorant of the harm attached to it, and so the purpose of restricting it to ignorance is to indicate that the believer does not engage in what he knows leads to harm.

His saying: ﴿Then repents after it﴾: that is, after his action, and rectifies what he corrupted by disobedience, so he returns to the right and performs obedience. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

On the first reading, "anna" and what follows it is the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, "so His command is that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." This is the choice of Sibawayh. Abu Hatim chose that the clause is in the nominative position as the subject, with an omitted predicate, as if it were said: "so for him is: 'indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.'" He said: because the subject is what follows the fa'.

As for the second reading, the clause is a resumptive sentence.

His saying: ﴿And thus We detail the signs﴾: that is, like that detailing We detail them. Tafsil (detailing) means clarification.

His saying: ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾.

The Kufans said: it is conjoined to an implied element: that is, "and thus We detail the signs, so that We may clarify to you and that it may become evident." Al-Nahhas said: this deletion is not needed.

When the way of the criminals becomes evident, the way of the believers has become evident as well.

Ibn Kathir said: "This hadith is gharib (strange), for this verse is Meccan, and al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyaynah only embraced Islam long after the Hijrah."

Sufyan said: "That is, the people of fiqh (understanding and jurisprudence)."

He did not respond to them with anything, so they departed. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you﴾ (the verse), so he called them and recited it to them."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "I was informed that His words ﴿Peace be upon you﴾ — when they entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ), he would begin the greeting of peace to them, saying: 'Peace be upon you.' And when he met them, he would do likewise."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Zayd, regarding His words ﴿That the way of the criminals may become clear﴾, that he said: "They are those who urge you to drive these people away."

Allah, glorified is He, commanded him (the Prophet ﷺ) to inform them, when their demands upon him and their obstinate insistence on the sending down of signs that would compel them to faith had multiplied, that he did not have the treasuries of Allah, so as to bring them the signs they had proposed. What is meant by "the treasuries of Allah" is the treasuries of His power, which encompass everything. He is also to tell them that he does not know the unseen, so as to inform them of it and make them aware of what will happen in the future of time. And he is to say to them, "I do not tell you that I am an angel, so that you may impose upon me acts that exceed custom and that no human can bear." There is nothing in this that indicates the angels are superior to the prophets. A group of the people of knowledge have occupied themselves with this question of superiority, though no religious or worldly benefit follows from it.

Rather, discussion of such a matter is among the preoccupations with what does not concern a person, and part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him. ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾: that is, I follow only what Allah reveals to me. Those who deny that the prophets exercised independent reasoning (ijtihad, the scholarly effort to derive rulings) have held to this, acting on what the restrictive form (al-qasr, the restriction of a predicate to a subject) in this verse conveys. The issue is codified in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh), and the evidence for it is well known. It is authentically related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "I have been given the Qur'an and the like of it with it."

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ This interrogative is for denial. What is meant is that the one who is astray and the one who is guided are not equal, or the Muslim and the disbelievers, or the one who follows what has been revealed to him and the one who does not follow it. The statement is an analogy. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ so that you may know the inequality between the two, for it is clear and is not obscured to one who has the least intelligence and the slightest reflection. The pronoun in "thereby" refers to what is revealed. It was said that it refers to Allah, and it was said that it refers to the Last Day.

He specified those who fear being gathered because warning affects them on account of the fear that has descended upon them, unlike one of the groups of disbelief who does not fear the gathering, due to his denial of it and his rejection of it, for such warning does not affect him.

It was said: the meaning of "fear" here is "know" and "be certain" that they will be gathered, so it includes every believer in resurrection from among the Muslims, the protected people (ahl al-dhimma, non-Muslim subjects under Muslim protection), and some of the polytheists. It was also said: the meaning of fear is its literal sense, and the meaning is that he warns with it those in whom fear of the gathering becomes evident upon hearing the Prophet (ﷺ) remind them, even if he was not affirming it originally, but he fears that what the Prophet (ﷺ) reported may be true. For whoever is like this, admonition is most effective with him and reminder most beneficial to him.

His saying: ﴿They have besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): that is, warn with it those who fear the gathering, while they have no protector who supports them, no helper who aids them, and no intercessor who intercedes for them apart from Allah. In this there is a refutation of those disbelievers who acknowledged the gathering and claimed that their forefathers would intercede for them, these being the People of the Book, or that their idols would intercede for them, these being the polytheists.

It was said: it means maintaining the congregational prayer. It was said: it means remembrance and recitation of the Qur'an. It was said: what is meant is supplication to Allah for bringing benefit and averting harm.

It was said: the mention of morning and evening means constancy and continuity in this. It was also said that it is on its apparent meaning. And ﴿seeking His face﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause.

The meaning is that they are sincere in their worship, seeking by it nothing but the face of Allah, the Exalted: that is, they turn with it toward Him and not toward anything else.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi concerning the verse, that he said: "They are the people of remembrance (ahl al-dhikr); do not drive them away from the remembrance."

Sufyan said: "That is, the people of fiqh (understanding and jurisprudence)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, that he said: "It means that He made some of them rich and some of them poor. The rich said to the poor: ﴿Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾" meaning: "Has Allah guided these?" They said this only mockingly and derisively.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾, that it means: "If they had any honour with Allah, this hardship would not have befallen them."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Maham, who said: "A people came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'We have committed great sins.' He did not respond to them with anything, so they departed. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you﴾ (the verse), so he called them and recited it to them."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "I was informed that His words ﴿Peace be upon you﴾ — when they entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ), he would begin the greeting of peace to them, saying: 'Peace be upon you.' And when he met them, he would do likewise."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir related from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And thus We detail the signs﴾, that he said: "We make the signs clear."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Zayd, regarding His words ﴿That the way of the criminals may become clear﴾, that he said: "They are those who urge you to drive these people away."

Allah, glorified is He, commanded him (the Prophet ﷺ) to inform them, when their demands upon him and their obstinate insistence on the sending down of signs that would compel them to faith had multiplied, that he did not have the treasuries of Allah, so as to bring them the signs they had proposed. What is meant by "the treasuries of Allah" is the treasuries of His power, which encompass everything. He is also to tell them that he does not know the unseen, so as to inform them of it and make them aware of what will happen in the future of time. And he is to say to them, "I do not tell you that I am an angel, so that you may impose upon me acts that exceed custom and that no human can bear." There is nothing in this that indicates the angels are superior to the prophets. A group of the people of knowledge have occupied themselves with this question of superiority, though no religious or worldly benefit follows from it.

Rather, discussion of such a matter is among the preoccupations with what does not concern a person, and part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him. ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾: that is, I follow only what Allah reveals to me. Those who deny that the prophets exercised independent reasoning (ijtihad, the scholarly effort to derive rulings) have held to this, acting on what the restrictive form (al-qasr, the restriction of a predicate to a subject) in this verse conveys. The issue is codified in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh), and the evidence for it is well known. It is authentically related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "I have been given the Qur'an and the like of it with it."

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ This interrogative is for denial. What is meant is that the one who is astray and the one who is guided are not equal, or the Muslim and the disbelievers, or the one who follows what has been revealed to him and the one who does not follow it. The statement is an analogy. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ so that you may know the inequality between the two, for it is clear and is not obscured to one who has the least intelligence and the slightest reflection. (p-٤٢١)

His saying: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾. Al-indhar (warning) means informing.

The pronoun in "thereby" refers to what is revealed. It was said that it refers to Allah, and it was said that it refers to the Last Day.

He specified those who fear being gathered because warning affects them on account of the fear that has descended upon them, unlike one of the groups of disbelief who does not fear the gathering, due to his denial of it and his rejection of it, for such warning does not affect him.

It was said: the meaning of "fear" here is "know" and "be certain" that they will be gathered, so it includes every believer in resurrection from among the Muslims, the protected people (ahl al-dhimma, non-Muslim subjects under Muslim protection), and some of the polytheists. It was also said: the meaning of fear is its literal sense, and the meaning is that he warns with it those in whom fear of the gathering becomes evident upon hearing the Prophet (ﷺ) remind them, even if he was not affirming it originally, but he fears that what the Prophet (ﷺ) reported may be true. For whoever is like this, admonition is most effective with him and reminder most beneficial to him.

His saying: ﴿They have besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): that is, warn with it those who fear the gathering, while they have no protector who supports them, no helper who aids them, and no intercessor who intercedes for them apart from Allah. In this there is a refutation of those disbelievers who acknowledged the gathering and claimed that their forefathers would intercede for them, these being the People of the Book, or that their idols would intercede for them, these being the polytheists.

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face﴾. Al-du'a' (supplication) here means worship in general. It was said: it means maintaining the congregational prayer. It was said: it means remembrance and recitation of the Qur'an. It was said: what is meant is supplication to Allah for bringing benefit and averting harm.

It was said: the mention of morning and evening means constancy and continuity in this. It was also said that it is on its apparent meaning. And ﴿seeking His face﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause.

The meaning is that they are sincere in their worship, seeking by it nothing but the face of Allah, the Exalted: that is, they turn with it toward Him and not toward anything else.

His saying: ﴿Upon you is not any of their account, and upon them is not any of your account﴾. This is a parenthetical statement between the prohibition and its answer, containing the negation of what would motivate the driving away. That is: the account of those whom you wished to drive away, in compliance with one who asked you to do so, is upon themselves, and nothing of it is upon you; and your account is upon yourself, and nothing of it is upon them. So why would you drive them away? This is on the supposition of the truth of the description of those who described them with His saying: ﴿And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us﴾ [Hud: 27], and who slandered their religion and lineage in your presence. How much more so when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commended them for worship and sincerity. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and His saying: ﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for﴾ [al-Najm: 39], and His saying: ﴿Their account is only upon my Lord﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 113].

His saying: ﴿So you would drive them away﴾ is the answer to the negation in His saying: ﴿Upon you is not any of their account﴾, and it is part of the parenthetical statement. That is: if the matter is so, then turn to them, sit with them, and do not drive them away, out of regard for the right of one who is not in their condition in religion and merit. The "min" in ﴿min hisabihim min shay'in﴾ is partitive, and the second is for emphasis, and likewise in ﴿wa ma min hisabika 'alayhim min shay'in﴾.

His saying: ﴿So you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is the answer to the prohibition, namely ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾. That is: if you did that, you would be among the wrongdoers. He is far from committing that, and this is only by way of allusion, lest anyone else among the Muslims, other than the Prophet (ﷺ), do likewise, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your work would surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]. It was said that ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is conjoined to ﴿so you would drive them away﴾ by way of causation, but the first is preferable.

His saying: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them by means of others﴾. That is: like that great trial, We tried some people by means of others. Fitna (trial) here means testing: that is, We dealt with them as testers deal. The lam in ﴿liyaqulu﴾ ("that they might say") indicates result (lam al-'aqibah): that is, so that the first group might say, pointing to the second group, "Are these the ones whom Allah has favored among us?" That is, He honored them by guiding them to the truth rather than us.

Al-Nahhas said: This is among the difficult points, for it is asked: how were they tried so that they would say this statement, which, if it was in the manner of denial, is disbelief? He answered with two answers. The first: that this was said by them in the manner of a question, not in the manner of denial. The second: that when they were tested by this, its consequence was this statement from them, like His saying: ﴿So the household of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas: 8].

His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ This interrogative is for affirmation. The meaning is that the basis of entitlement to the blessings of Allah, glorified is He, is gratitude, and He is most knowing of those who are grateful to Him. So what is the matter with you that you object out of ignorance and deny the grace?

His saying: ﴿And when those come to you who believe in Our signs﴾: they are those whom Allah forbade him to drive away, and they are the oppressed among the believers, as its explanation will come. ﴿Say: Peace be upon you.﴾ Allah commanded him to say this statement to them, as a comforting of their hearts and an honoring of them.

Al-salam and al-salama have the same meaning, so the meaning of "salamun 'alaykum" is: may Allah keep you safe.

After the revelation of this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he saw them, would greet them first with peace. It was also said that this peace is from Allah: that is, convey to them peace from us.

His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾: that is, He made this obligatory as an obligation of grace and kindness. It was also said that He wrote this in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

It was said: this is among what Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to convey to those to whom He commanded him to convey the greeting, as good tidings of the vastness of Allah's forgiveness and the greatness of His mercy.

His saying: ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, and Nafi' read "annahu" with a fatha on the alif (anna), and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, this clause is a substitute (badal) for "mercy": that is, your Lord has prescribed for Himself that whoever of you does (and so on to the end).

On the second reading, this clause explains "mercy" by way of a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), and the position of "bi-jahalah" (in ignorance) is accusative as a circumstantial clause: that is, he did it while being ignorant.

It was said: the meaning is that he acted as the ignorant act, for whoever does what leads to harm in the outcome, while knowing or suspecting it, has acted as the people of ignorance and foolishness act, not as the people of wisdom and prudence act. It was also said: the meaning is that he did it while ignorant of the harm attached to it, and so the purpose of restricting it to ignorance is to indicate that the believer does not engage in what he knows leads to harm.

His saying: ﴿Then repents after it﴾: that is, after his action, and rectifies what he corrupted by disobedience, so he returns to the right and performs obedience. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim (p-٤٢٢) read "fa-annahu" with a fatha on the hamza, and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, "anna" and what follows it is the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, "so His command is that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." This is the choice of Sibawayh. Abu Hatim chose that the clause is in the nominative position as the subject, with an omitted predicate, as if it were said: "so for him is: 'indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.'" He said: because the subject is what follows the fa'.

As for the second reading, the clause is a resumptive sentence.

His saying: ﴿And thus We detail the signs﴾: that is, like that detailing We detail them. Tafsil (detailing) means clarification.

The meaning is that Allah has made clear to them what they need of the matters of religion and has explained to them the ruling for every group.

His saying: ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾.

The Kufans said: it is conjoined to an implied element: that is, "and thus We detail the signs, so that We may clarify to you and that it may become evident." Al-Nahhas said: this deletion is not needed.

It was also said that the entry of the waw is for conjunction according to meaning. "Li-tastabina" has been read with the second person (ta, feminine/upper) and with the third person (ya, lower). The address in the second person is to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, that you, O Muhammad, may make evident the way of the criminals. "Sabil" is in the accusative in the reading of Nafi'. As for the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs, with the nominative, the verb is attributed to "sabil." As for the third person, the verb is also attributed to "sabil," and this is the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Shu'ba with the nominative. When the way of the criminals becomes evident, the way of the believers has become evident as well.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾, that he said: "The blind is the disbeliever who is blind to the right of Allah, His command, and His blessings upon him. The seeing is the servant who is a believer, who sees with beneficial sight, so he affirms the oneness of Allah alone, acts in obedience to his Lord, and benefits from what Allah has given him."

Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while with him were Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab, and others of the weak Muslims. They said: 'O Muhammad, are you content with these from among your people?' ﴿Are these the ones whom Allah has favored among us?﴾ Shall we be followers of these? Drive them away from us, for perhaps if you drive them away we will follow you.' So Allah revealed concerning them the Qur'an: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾"

This occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) has been related at length by Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir, from Ikrimah, and in it: those who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) were ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, Qarazah ibn ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Nawfal, al-Harith ibn ʿAmir ibn Nawfal, and Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi ibn al-Khiyar ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of the disbelievers from ʿAbd Manaf.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Majah, Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nuʿaym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalail also related it from Khabbab, who said: "al-Aqraʿ ibn Habis al-Tamimi and ʿUyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari came," and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, at length.

Ibn Kathir said: "This hadith is gharib (strange), for this verse is Meccan, and al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyaynah only embraced Islam long after the Hijrah."

Muslim, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and others related from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning six: myself, ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, Bilal, a man from Hudhayl, and two men whom I will not name. The polytheists said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Drive these away from you; they will not dare to act boldly against us.' So there came into the soul of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) what Allah willed to come, and he spoke to himself, and Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾."

Reports explaining the occasion of revelation with a meaning consistent with what we have mentioned have also been narrated.

It was said: this is among what Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to convey to those to whom He commanded him to convey the greeting, as good tidings of the vastness of Allah's forgiveness and the greatness of His mercy.

His saying: ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, and Nafi' read "annahu" with a fatha on the alif (anna), and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, this clause is a substitute (badal) for "mercy": that is, your Lord has prescribed for Himself that whoever of you does (and so on to the end).

On the second reading, this clause explains "mercy" by way of a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), and the position of "bi-jahalah" (in ignorance) is accusative as a circumstantial clause: that is, he did it while being ignorant.

It was said: the meaning is that he acted as the ignorant act, for whoever does what leads to harm in the outcome, while knowing or suspecting it, has acted as the people of ignorance and foolishness act, not as the people of wisdom and prudence act. It was also said: the meaning is that he did it while ignorant of the harm attached to it, and so the purpose of restricting it to ignorance is to indicate that the believer does not engage in what he knows leads to harm.

His saying: ﴿Then repents after it﴾: that is, after his action, and rectifies what he corrupted by disobedience, so he returns to the right and performs obedience. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim (p-٤٢٢) read "fa-annahu" with a fatha on the hamza, and the rest read it with a kasra.

On the first reading, "anna" and what follows it is the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, "so His command is that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." This is the choice of Sibawayh. Abu Hatim chose that the clause is in the nominative position as the subject, with an omitted predicate, as if it were said: "so for him is: 'indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.'" He said: because the subject is what follows the fa'.

As for the second reading, the clause is a resumptive sentence.

His saying: ﴿And thus We detail the signs﴾: that is, like that detailing We detail them. Tafsil (detailing) means clarification.

The meaning is that Allah has made clear to them what they need of the matters of religion and has explained to them the ruling for every group.

His saying: ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾.

The Kufans said: it is conjoined to an implied element: that is, "and thus We detail the signs, so that We may clarify to you and that it may become evident." Al-Nahhas said: this deletion is not needed.

It was also said that the entry of the waw is for conjunction according to meaning. "Li-tastabina" has been read with the second person (ta, feminine/upper) and with the third person (ya, lower). The address in the second person is to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, that you, O Muhammad, may make evident the way of the criminals. "Sabil" is in the accusative in the reading of Nafi'. As for the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs, with the nominative, the verb is attributed to "sabil." As for the third person, the verb is also attributed to "sabil," and this is the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Shu'ba with the nominative. When the way of the criminals becomes evident, the way of the believers has become evident as well.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾, that he said: "The blind is the disbeliever who is blind to the right of Allah, His command, and His blessings upon him. The seeing is the servant who is a believer, who sees with beneficial sight, so he affirms the oneness of Allah alone, acts in obedience to his Lord, and benefits from what Allah has given him."

Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while with him were Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab, and others of the weak Muslims. They said: 'O Muhammad, are you content with these from among your people?' ﴿Are these the ones whom Allah has favored among us?﴾ Shall we be followers of these? Drive them away from us, for perhaps if you drive them away we will follow you.' So Allah revealed concerning them the Qur'an: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾"

This occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) has been related at length by Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir, from Ikrimah, and in it: those who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) were ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, Qarazah ibn ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Nawfal, al-Harith ibn ʿAmir ibn Nawfal, and Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi ibn al-Khiyar ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of the disbelievers from ʿAbd Manaf.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Majah, Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nuʿaym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalail also related it from Khabbab, who said: "al-Aqraʿ ibn Habis al-Tamimi and ʿUyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari came," and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, at length.

Ibn Kathir said: "This hadith is gharib (strange), for this verse is Meccan, and al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyaynah only embraced Islam long after the Hijrah."

Muslim, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and others related from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning six: myself, ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, Bilal, a man from Hudhayl, and two men whom I will not name. The polytheists said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Drive these away from you; they will not dare to act boldly against us.' So there came into the soul of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) what Allah willed to come, and he spoke to himself, and Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾."

Reports explaining the occasion of revelation with a meaning consistent with what we have mentioned have also been narrated.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿morning and evening﴾, that he said: "It means the obligatory prayer (al-salah al-maktubah)."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid, who said: "The obligatory prayer is the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi concerning the verse, that he said: "They are the people of remembrance (ahl al-dhikr); do not drive them away from the remembrance."

Sufyan said: "That is, the people of fiqh (understanding and jurisprudence)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, that he said: "It means that He made some of them rich and some of them poor. The rich said to the poor: ﴿Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾" meaning: "Has Allah guided these?" They said this only mockingly and derisively.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?﴾, that it means: "If they had any honour with Allah, this hardship would not have befallen them."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Maham, who said: "A people came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'We have committed great sins.' He did not respond to them with anything, so they departed. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you﴾ (the verse), so he called them and recited it to them."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "I was informed that His words ﴿Peace be upon you﴾ — when they entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ), he would begin the greeting of peace to them, saying: 'Peace be upon you.' And when he met them, he would do likewise."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir related from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And thus We detail the signs﴾, that he said: "We make the signs clear."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Zayd, regarding His words ﴿That the way of the criminals may become clear﴾, that he said: "They are those who urge you to drive these people away."

(p. 423) **His saying: ﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden﴾**. God, glorified be He, commanded him to return to addressing the disbelievers and to inform them that he has been forbidden to worship what they call upon and worship besides God. That is, God forbade him from this, turned him away from it, and restrained him. Then God, glorified be He, commanded him to say to them: ﴿"I will not follow your desires"﴾, that is, I will not take the path you have taken in your religion, following desires and proceeding according to what corrupt aims require, which result in falling into misguidance.

**His saying: ﴿"Then I would have gone astray"﴾**, that is, if I followed your desires in what you have demanded of me, namely worshipping your deities and driving away those whom you wish to drive away, ﴿"and I would not be among the guided"﴾ if I did that. This nominal sentence (*jumlah ismiyyah*) is conjoined to the sentence before it. Its being nominal after that verbal sentence (*jumlah fiʿliyyah*) indicates permanence and continuity. The verb "ḍalaltu" has been read with the vowel of the *lām* both fatḥah and kasrah, and both are dialects.

Abu ʿAmr said: "ḍillitu" with kasrah on the *lām* is the dialect of Tamim, and it is the recitation of Ibn Wathhāb and Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif. The first (fatḥah) is more correct and more eloquent, because it is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, and it is the recitation of the majority.

Al-Jawharī said: "ḍalāl" and "ḍalālah" are the opposite of "rashād" (right guidance), and "ḍalaltu, aḍillu" (I went astray, I go astray).

God, Exalted, says: ﴿"If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment"﴾ (Sabaʾ 34:50). He said: this, meaning the fatḥah form, is the dialect of Najd and it is the more eloquent, while the people of al-ʿĀliyah say "ḍillitu" with kasrah, "aḍillu."

**His saying: ﴿"Indeed I am upon a clear proof from my Lord"﴾**. "Al-bayyinah" means proof and evidence: that is, I am upon a demonstrative proof from my Lord and certainty, not upon desire or doubt. God, glorified be He, commanded him to make clear to them that what he is upon in worshipping his Lord is based on a demonstrative, certain proof, unlike what they are upon, which is following weak dubious notions and corrupt doubts that have no basis except mere false desires.

**His saying: ﴿"And you have denied it"﴾**, that is, denied "him" (the Lord), or the punishment, or the Qur'an, or the clear proof. The masculine pronoun is used in accordance with the meaning.

This sentence is either a circumstantial clause (*ḥāliyyah*) with *qad* implied, meaning "while in fact you have denied it," or a resumptive independent sentence (*jumlah mustaʾnafah*) explaining what they are upon of denial of what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, brought of clear arguments and manifest proofs.

**His saying: ﴿"What you are hastening is not with me"﴾**. He informed them that he did not have what they were hastening of punishment. For, because of their excessive denial, they were hastening its descent mockingly, like His saying: ﴿"Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments as you claim"﴾ (al-Isrāʾ 17:92), and their saying: ﴿"O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky"﴾ (al-Anfāl 8:32), and their saying: ﴿"When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ (Sabaʾ 34:29). It has also been said that ﴿"What you are hastening is not with me"﴾ refers to the signs you suggest to me.

**His saying: ﴿"Judgment belongs only to God"﴾**, that is, judgment in all things belongs only to God, glorified be He, and among that is what you are hastening of punishment or of the suggested signs.

What is meant is the decisive judgment between truth and falsehood.

**His saying: ﴿"He relates the truth"﴾**. Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and ʿĀṣim read *yaqussu* with the *qāf* and an unpointed *ṣād*. The rest read *yaqḍī* with the pointed *ḍād* and a *yā'*, and so also read ʿAlī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab. It is written in the muṣḥaf without a *yā'*.

According to the first recitation, it is from *qaṣaṣ* (narrative): that is, He relates the true narratives; or from *qaṣṣa atharahu* (he followed his track): that is, He follows the truth in what He judges. According to the second recitation, it is from *qaḍāʾ* (judgment): that is, He issues the true judgment among His servants. "Al-ḥaqq" is in the accusative as a direct object, or as an attribute of an omitted verbal noun: that is, He judges the true judgment, or He relates the true narrative. ﴿"And He is the best of deciders"﴾, that is, between truth and falsehood, by what He decides among His servants and makes clear to them in His Book.

Then God, glorified be He, commanded him to say to them: ﴿"If I had what you are hastening, the matter would have been decided between me and you"﴾, that is, what you seek to hasten by having its descent be within my power and capacity. ﴿"The matter would have been decided between me and you"﴾, that is, God would have decided the matter between us by sending it down upon you at my request and my demand for it. Or the meaning is: if the punishment you seek and hasten were with me and in my grasp, I would have sent it down upon you, and at that point the matter would be decided between me and you. ﴿"And God knows best the wrongdoers"﴾, and the time at which their punishment descends, and what His will requires of delaying it as a gradual respite (*istidrāj*) for them and as an excuse made to them.

**His saying: ﴿"With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He"﴾**. *Al-mafātiḥ* is the plural of *mafḥ* with a fatḥah, which is the storehouse, that is: with Him are the storehouses of the unseen. He made for unseen matters storehouses in which they are stored, by way of metaphor (*istiʿārah*). Or it is the plural of *mifḥ* with a kasrah on the *mīm*, which is *miftāḥ* (key); He made for unseen matters keys by which one reaches what is in the storehouses of them, also by way of metaphor. What supports that it is the plural of *mifḥ* with kasrah is the recitation of Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ: *wa-ʿindahu mafātīḥu al-ghayb* (with *mafātīḥ*, the plural of *miftāḥ*). The meaning is: with Him, glorified be He, alone are the storehouses of the unseen, or the keys by which the storehouses are reached.

His saying: ﴿"None knows them but He"﴾ is a sentence emphasizing the content of the first sentence, and that no one among His creatures has knowledge of any of the unseen matters that God has reserved for Himself. Included under this verse is knowledge of the punishment the disbelievers are hastening, as the context indicates in a preliminary way.

In this noble verse is a refutation of the falsehoods of soothsayers (*kuhhān*), astrologers (*munajjimīn*), geomancers (*ramliyyūn*), and others among the claimants to what is not their concern, what does not fall within their power, and what their knowledge does not encompass. Islam and its people have been afflicted by a wicked people of these misguided kinds and debased types, and they have gained nothing from their lies and falsehoods except the evil path mentioned in the saying of the truthful one whose word is trusted, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace: "Whoever comes to a soothsayer or an astrologer has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad."

**His saying: ﴿"And He knows what is on the land and in the sea"﴾**. He singled out these two for mention because they are among the greatest of God's creations, that is, He knows what is in them of animal and inanimate things with detailed knowledge, nothing of it hidden from Him. Or He singled them out because they are what people most observe and most look forward to knowing what is in them. ﴿"Not a leaf falls but He knows it"﴾, that is, of the leaves of the tree. This is a specification after a generalization: He knows it, and He knows the time of its falling and its place. It has been said that the "leaf" here refers to what the lifespans and provisions are written on. Al-Naqqāsh reported from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad that "leaf" here means a miscarried child of the children of Adam. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: this is a view that follows the way of symbolic interpretation, is not authentically transmitted from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and should not be paid attention to. ﴿"Nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth"﴾, that is, in dark places. It has been said: in the depths of the earth. ﴿"Nor anything moist or dry"﴾, with the genitive (*khafḍ*) as a conjunction with "ḥabbah" (grain), which is conjoined to "waraqah" (leaf).

Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, al-Ḥasan, and others read it in the nominative, as a conjunction with the position of "min waraqah" (from a leaf). The attribute of moistness and dryness encompasses all existing things.

**His saying: ﴿"Except that it is in a clear Book"﴾**. This is the Preserved Tablet (*al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ*), so this sentence is a comprehensive apposition (*badal ishtimāl*) for "illā yaʿlamuhā" (except that He knows it). It has been said that it is an expression for His knowledge, so this sentence is a full apposition (*badal kull*) for that sentence.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh reported from Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, regarding His saying: ﴿"Indeed I am upon a clear proof from my Lord"﴾, that he said: "upon trust (*thiqah*)."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Abū al-Shaykh reported from ʿIkrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿"The matter would have been decided between me and you"﴾, that he said: "the Hour would have been established."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from al-Suddī, regarding His saying: ﴿"And with Him are the keys of the unseen"﴾, that he said: "He says: the treasures of the unseen."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿"And with Him are the keys of the unseen"﴾, that he said: "They are five," ﴿"Indeed God has knowledge of the Hour"﴾ up to His saying: "All-Knowing, All-Aware" (Luqmān 31:34).

Aḥmad, al-Bukhārī, and others reported from Ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The keys of the unseen are five, none knows them but God: none knows what will be tomorrow but God; none knows what the wombs bear (*taghīḍu al-arḥām*) but God; none knows when the rain will come but God; no soul knows in what land it will die but God; and none knows when the Hour will be established but God."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿"Not a leaf falls but He knows it"﴾, that he said: "There is no tree on land or sea but that there is an angel with it who records what falls of its leaves."

Abū al-Shaykh reported similarly from Mujāhid.

Abū al-Shaykh reported from Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah regarding ﴿"Not a leaf falls"﴾, that he said: "For God, blessed and exalted, there is a tree beneath the Throne; there is no created being except that it has a leaf on it. When its leaf falls, its spirit leaves its body. That is His saying: ﴿'Not a leaf falls but He knows it.'"

Al-Khaṭīb reported in his *Tārīkh* with a weak chain from Ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "There is no seed upon the earth nor fruit upon trees except that upon it is written: 'In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, this is the provision of so-and-so son of so-and-so.' That is His saying, exalted be He: 'Not a leaf falls...'" to the end of the verse.

It was also transmitted by Ibn Yazīd ibn Hārūn from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, and he mentioned it.

Abū al-Shaykh reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he recited this verse: ﴿"Nor anything moist or dry"﴾, and said: "The moist and the dry of everything."
