The clause ﴿and the life of this world has deceived them﴾ is coordinated with "they have taken," meaning: it deceived them until they preferred it over the Hereafter, denied the resurrection, and said: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected﴾.

His saying: ﴿And warn by it, lest a soul be delivered to destruction for what it has earned﴾. The pronoun in "bihi" (by it) refers to the Qur'an or to the reckoning.

Ibsāl means a person surrendering himself to destruction. From it comes "absaltu waladī," meaning I pledged my son in blood, because its outcome is destruction.

Al-Nābigha said:

*We pledged Āmir as a pledge for the Afāqa, for what was a pledge at al-Dardāʾ, so he was delivered up.*

That is, he perished. Al-Dardāʾ is a battalion that was well known among them by this name. So the meaning: warn by it, lest or for fear or dread that a soul perish for what it has earned, that is, be pledged and delivered to ruin. The original sense of ibsāl is restraint, and from it comes "shujāʿ bāsil," meaning a brave man who holds back from his opponent.

His saying: ﴿And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it﴾. Here "ʿadl" means ransom.

The meaning: even if that soul which has been delivered to destruction offers every ransom, that ransom will not be accepted from it, so that by it it might be saved from destruction. The subject of "yuʾkhadh" (be accepted) is a pronoun referring to ʿadl, since it carries the sense of the thing given as ransom, as in His saying: ﴿nor will any ransom be accepted from it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:48]. It was also said: its subject is "minhā" (from it), because here ʿadl is a verbal noun that cannot take a verb as its subject. "Kulla ʿadl" is in the accusative as a verbal noun: that is, ransom of every kind.

The demonstrative in His saying ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who took their religion as amusement and play, and its predicate is ﴿those who have been delivered to destruction for what they have earned﴾: that is, these people who took their religion as amusement and play are those who were delivered to destruction for what they earned. And ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾ is an answer to an assumed question, as if it were said: what is the condition of these people? So it is said: ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾, which is hot water. A similar expression is His saying: ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads﴾ [Al-Ḥajj 22:19]. Here it is a drink they drink, which cuts their intestines to pieces.

His saying: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides God, what neither benefits us nor harms us?﴾ God, glorified is He, commanded him to tell them this statement. The interrogative is for rebuke: that is, how can we call upon idols besides God, which do not benefit us in any way of benefit, if we want benefit from them, and which we do not fear the harm of in any way? Whoever is like this does not deserve worship. ﴿And be turned back on our heels﴾ is coordinated with "we call upon."

"Aʿqāb" is the plural of ʿaqib: that is, how can we call upon one who is like that and return to the misguidance from which God has brought us out?

Abū ʿUbayda said: it is said of one who is turned back from his need and does not obtain it, "he was turned back on his heels."

Al-Mubarrad said: we are repaid with evil after good. Its origin is from successive following (muʿāqaba) and "ʿuqbā," which are what follows something and must come after it. From it comes ﴿And the final outcome is for the God-fearing﴾ [Al-Qaṣaṣ 28:83]. From it comes ʿaqib (heel) of a man, and from it ʿuqūba (punishment), because it follows the sin.

His saying: ﴿Like one whom the devils have enticed on the earth﴾. Hawā (to fall) means to hasten toward something.

Al-Zajjāj said: it is from the desire of the soul, that is, Satan adorned his desire for him, and ﴿the devils have enticed him﴾ means they carried him off. The kāf in "ka-lladhī" is either an adjective to a deleted verbal noun, meaning: we are turned back upon our heels in a turning like that of one who..., or in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the subject of "nuraddu": that is, we are turned back (p-428) in a state of resembling him whom the devils have enticed, that is, the rebellious jinn have carried him off after he had been among mankind.

The majority read "istahawathu" (with the feminine pronoun). Ḥamza read "istahwāhu" in the masculine form, agreeing with the masculine collective noun.

Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan read "istahwāhu al-shayṭān" (the devil enticed him), and it is the same in the reading of Ubayy. "Ḥayrān" is a circumstantial state: that is, while he is bewildered and lost, not knowing how to act. Ḥayrān is one who does not find his way to any direction. One says "ḥāra ḥayratan wa-ḥayrūratan" when he wanders about. From this the stagnant water that has no outlet is named "ḥāʾir."

His saying: ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance﴾: this is a description of ḥayrān or a circumstantial clause: that is, he has companions who call him to guidance, saying to him, "Come to us," but he does not answer them and does not follow their guidance.

His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of God is the guidance﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to tell them: ﴿Indeed, the guidance of God﴾, that is, His religion which He has chosen for His servants, ﴿is the guidance﴾, and whatever is other than it is falsehood. ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:85]. "And we are commanded" is coordinated with the nominal sentence: that is, among what God commanded him to say. The lām in "li-nuslima" is the lām of cause, and what is caused is the command: that is, we were commanded for the purpose that we submit to the Lord of the worlds.

Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is we were commanded to submit, because the Arabs say "amartuka li-tadhhaba" (I commanded you so that you go) and "bi-an tadhhaba" with the same meaning.

Al-Naḥḥās said: I heard Ibn Kaysān say: it is the lām of the genitive (lām al-khafḍ).

His saying: ﴿And that you establish prayer and fear Him﴾ is coordinated with "li-nuslima," in the sense of "we were commanded to submit and to establish prayer." It may also be coordinated with "yadʿūnahu" in meaning: that is, they call him to guidance and call him to establish prayer.

﴿And He is the One to whom you will be gathered﴾, so how do you oppose His command?

﴿And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾: creating them with truth, or while the creation is in truth. So how do you worship idols, which are themselves created?

He said: ﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is, [His word is the truth]﴾. ﴿His word is the truth﴾ means: remember the day when He says, "Be," and it is; or, fear the day when He says, "Be," and it is. It was also said that it is a conjunction (ʿatf) with the pronoun in *wa-ittaquhu* (﴿and fear Him﴾). It was also said that *yawma* (the day) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf) governed by the sense of the clause ﴿His word is the truth﴾, and the meaning is: His command, which relates to things. *Al-Ḥaqq* (the truth) means: the one for whom it is witnessed that it is true. It was also said that *qawluhu* (His word) is the subject (mubtadaʾ), *al-ḥaqq* is its qualifier (ṣifah), and ﴿and the day He says, "Be," and it is﴾ is its predicate (khabar), placed before it. The meaning is: His word, qualified by truth, exists on the day when He says, "Be," and it is. It was also said that *qawluhu* is raised by *yakūnu* (it is), and *al-ḥaqq* is its qualifier, that is: on the day He says "Be," His word, the truth, will be.

Ibn ʿĀmir read *fa-nakūnu* with the nūn (we), and this indicates the speed of the reckoning. The rest read it with the yāʾ (he), which is the correct reading.

He said: ﴿And His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown﴾. The adverbial (ẓarf) is in the accusative, governed by what precedes it, that is: His is the dominion on this day. It was also said that it is a substitution (badal) for the first *yawm* (day). *Al-Ṣūr* (the Trumpet) is a horn into which the first blast is blown for annihilation and the second for re-creation. Al-Jawharī likewise said that *al-ṣūr* is the horn. The rajaz poet said:

*"We struck them on the morning of the two hosts, a violent strike, not like the strike of the two horns."*

*Al-Ṣūr* is pronounced with a ḍammah or a kasrah on the ṣād, as dialectal forms. It is reported from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd that he read *yawma yunfakhu fī al-ṣuwar* with the wāw vowelled, as the plural of *ṣūrah* (form), and the intended meaning is creation. Abū ʿUbaydah said: this, although possible, is rejected by what is in the Book and the Sunnah. Al-Farrāʾ said: *kun fa-yakūn* is said to refer to the Trumpet specifically, that is: and on the day He says to the Trumpet, "Be," and it is.

He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾. *ʿĀlimu* is raised because it is a qualifier of *alladhī khalaqa al-samāwāti wa-al-arḍ* (He who created the heavens and the earth). It is also permissible that it be raised by supposing an implied subject: that is, He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. It is reported from some of them that he read *yanfukhu* with the active form, and on this reading the subject may be ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾. It is also permissible that it be raised by an implied verb, as Sībawayh cited:

*"At your call, Yazid, a suppliant for a dispute, and one who is struck by what the calamities cast down."*

That is: *yubkīhi mukhtabiṭun* (one who is struck weeps for him).

Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read *ʿālimi* in the genitive, as a substitution (badal) for the pronoun in *lahu al-mulk* (His is the dominion). ﴿And He is the Wise﴾ in all that proceeds from Him, ﴿the Aware of everything﴾.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddī, regarding His saying ﴿And your people denied it﴾: he said, Quraysh denied the Qur'an. ﴿And it is the truth﴾. As for *al-wakīl* (the guardian), it means the one who preserves. As for ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾, the news of the people became fixed on the day of Badr by what He had promised them of punishment.

An-Naḥḥās narrated in his work on abrogation (naskh) from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾: he said, this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword (*āyat al-sayf*): ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5].

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: he said, it means a reality (ḥaqīqah).

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: its punishment is withheld until its sin is committed, then its punishment is released.

Ibn Jarīr narrated through al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: he said, it is an action and a reality, both what occurred of it in this world and what occurred of it in the Hereafter.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them﴾ and similar in the Qur'an: he said, Allah commanded the believers to unity, forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them that those before them were destroyed only through contention and disputes concerning the religion of Allah.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses﴾: he said, they mock them. He forbade Muḥammad (ﷺ) to sit with them, except if he forgets; when reminded, he should stand up. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿So do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn that he held that this verse was revealed concerning the people of desires (ahl al-ahwāʾ).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Abū Nuʿaym in *al-Ḥilyah* narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, who said: Do not sit with the people of disputes, for they are those who engage in vain talk concerning the verses of Allah.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, who said: the companions of desires are among those who engage in vain talk concerning the verses of Allah.

Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Muqātil, who said: when the polytheists in Mecca heard the Qur'an from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), they engaged in vain talk and mocked. The Muslims said: their company is not suitable for us, we fear that we would go out when we hear their words and sit with them, and then we would not blame them. So Allah revealed this verse.

Abū al-Shaykh also narrated from al-Suddī that he said: this verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

An-Naḥḥās narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿And upon those who fear Allah there is nothing of their reckoning﴾: he said, this Meccan verse was abrogated by the Medinan verse, which is His saying: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected and mocked, do not sit with them﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 140], and so on.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And upon those who fear Allah there is nothing of their reckoning﴾: if they sit, but they should not sit.

Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, that a group was brought to him who had sat drinking with a man who was fasting. He struck them and said: do not sit with them until they engage in talk other than that.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding His saying ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion﴾: he said, it is like His saying: ﴿Leave Me with whom I created alone﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11], meaning it is for threat (tahdīd).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Abū Dāwūd in his work on abrogation narrated from Qatādah regarding this verse: he said, it was abrogated by the verse of the sword.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from him regarding ﴿amusement and diversion﴾: he said, eating and drinking.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿lest a soul be delivered to ruin (an tubsala)﴾: he said, lest it be disgraced. And regarding ﴿they were delivered to ruin (ubsilū)﴾: he said, they were disgraced.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from him regarding ﴿They were delivered to ruin for what they earned﴾: he said, they were handed over for their misdeeds.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated from him regarding ﴿Say, "Shall we call upon other than Allah"﴾: he said, this is a parable that Allah struck for the idols and for the callers who call to other than Allah.

As for His saying ﴿like one whom the devils have lured in the earth﴾: it means they misled him. They are the ghouls (ghīlān) who call him by his name and his father's name and his grandfather's name, so he follows them and thinks he is in something, and in the morning they have cast him into destruction. Perhaps they eat him, or they cast him into a desert wasteland where he perishes of thirst. This is the likeness of one who answers the gods that are worshipped other than Allah.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated from him regarding ﴿like one whom the devils have lured﴾: he said, it is the man who does not respond to the guidance of Allah. He is the man who obeys the devil, acts in the earth with disobedience, deviates from the truth and strays from it. ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance﴾ and claim that what they command him is guidance. Allah says this about their allies among mankind: ﴿Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of Allah﴾, and misguidance is what the jinn call to.

Ibn al-Mubārak in *al-Zuhd*, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī (who graded it ḥasan), al-Nasāʾī, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Ḥākim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Baʿth* narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the Trumpet, and he said: it is a horn into which it is blown." The narrations concerning the manner of the blowing are established in the books of hadith, and we have no need to cite them here.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: he means that the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed is the One who blows into the Trumpet.

**Verse 68 onward**

His saying: ﴿But your people have denied it﴾. The pronoun refers either to the Qur'an or to the punishment.

"His people" who deny are the Quraysh. It was also said that they are every stubborn opponent. The clause ﴿while it is the truth﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl): that is, they denied the Qur'an or the punishment while it is true.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read "wa-kadhdhabat" with the feminine ta' (the verb agreeing with a feminine noun).

﴿Say: I am not a guardian over you﴾: that is, I am not a watcher over your deeds so that I would requite you for them.

It was said: this verse is abrogated (mansūkha) by the verse of fighting. It was also said: it is not abrogated, since their belief was not within his power.

His saying: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾: that is, for every matter there is a time in which it occurs.

Al-naba' is the thing about which news is given. It was also said that the meaning is: for every deed there is a recompense.

Al-Zajjāj said: it may be a threat to them with what will befall them in this world. Al-Ḥasan said: this is a threat from God to the disbelievers, because they did not acknowledge the resurrection. ﴿And you will soon know﴾ that it has come about and descended upon them, just as they knew on the day of Badr when what the Prophet (ﷺ) had threatened them with came to pass.

His saying: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them﴾. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), or to anyone suited to it.

Al-khawḍ (vain engagement) originally means wading in water. Then it was used for the depths of things that are unknown, by analogy with the depths of water, so it was borrowed from the sensible to the intelligible. It was also said that it is derived from mixing: everything you wade into you have mixed, and from it comes "khāḍa al-māʾ bi-l-ʿasal" (he mixed water with honey).

The meaning: when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, through denial, rejection and mockery, leave them and do not sit with them to hear such a grave wrong, until they engage in a discourse other than it. God, glorified is He, commanded him to turn away from the people of gatherings in which the signs of God are belittled, until they move on to discussing something else.

In this verse there is a great admonition for those who tolerate sitting with innovators (mubtadiʿa) who distort the speech of God, toy with His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and reduce these to their misguided desires and corrupt innovations. If one does not object to them or change what they are engaged in, then at the very least one should abandon sitting with them, and that is easy for him, not difficult.

They may make his presence with them, even while he is free from what they are involved in, a pretext by which they mislead the common people, so that his presence brings an additional harm beyond merely hearing the wrong.

We have witnessed from these cursed gatherings what cannot be counted. We have stood up in support of the truth and in repelling falsehood with what we were able to do and what our capacity reached. Whoever truly knows this purified Sharia will know that sitting with the people of misguided innovation carries a harm many times greater than sitting with one who disobeys God by committing some of the forbidden acts. This is especially so for one whose feet are not firmly planted in the knowledge of the Book and the Sunnah, for he may well be struck by their lies and nonsense, which are as manifestly false as can be. Then something will take root in his heart that is hard to cure and difficult to repel, so he acts upon it for the rest of his life and meets God with it, believing it to be the truth while it is among the most false of falsehoods and the most reprehensible of wrongs.

His saying: ﴿And if Satan causes you to forget, do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾. (Immā) here is the conditional particle, and it is usually followed by the emphatic nūn, though rarely not. From this is the poet's saying:

*If an enemy overtakes you in his own dwellings one day, then say: how can he rise and prevail?*

Ibn ʿAbbās read "yunassīka" with a doubled sīn. Similarly is the poet's saying:

*Indolence often makes you forget some of what you need.*

The meaning: if Satan has caused you to forget to rise and leave them, then ﴿do not sit after the reminder﴾, when you have remembered, ﴿with the wrongdoing people﴾, that is, those who wronged themselves by mocking the signs and denying them.

It was said: although the apparent address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), what is intended is an indirect warning to his community, because he is exempt from Satan causing him to forget. It was also said: there is no basis for this, since forgetting is permissible for him, as the authentic traditions have stated: "I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me," and similar.

His saying: ﴿Nor is there upon those who are God-fearing any account of them at all﴾: that is, upon those who fear God and avoid sitting with the disbelievers when they engage in vain talk concerning the signs of God, there is no reckoning for the disbelievers at all.

It was also said: the meaning is that upon those who fear God there is nothing for what occurs from them of vain talk concerning the signs of God during their sitting with them. According to this interpretation, the verse grants a concession to the God-fearing believers to sit with the disbelievers when they are compelled to do so, as will be mentioned when the occasion of revelation is recounted.

It was said: this concession was at the beginning of Islam, when the circumstances were those of taqiyya (dissimulation). Then God's saying was revealed: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the signs of God being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a discourse other than that﴾, and this abrogated that (naskh).

His saying: ﴿But it is a reminder, that perhaps they may fear God﴾. The word "dhikrā" (reminder) is in an accusative position as a verbal noun, or in a nominative position as a subject whose predicate is omitted: that is, "but upon them is a reminder."

Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "but this is a reminder."

The meaning, as an exception from the preceding negation, is: but upon them is the reminder to the disbelievers, through admonition and explanation to them that this is not permissible.

As for the first interpretation: merely avoiding the gatherings of those who engage in vain talk concerning the signs of God does not remove the obligation to command the right and forbid the wrong.

As for the second interpretation: the concession to sit does not remove the obligation of reminding, ﴿that perhaps they may fear God﴾ from vain talk concerning the signs of God, if the reminder from you reaches them.

As for making the pronoun refer to the God-fearing, this is very far-fetched.

His saying: ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and play﴾: that is, leave these people who have taken the religion, which they were obliged to act upon and enter into, as amusement and play. Do not hang your heart on them, for they are people of obstinacy, even though you are commanded to convey the proof to them.

It was said: this verse is abrogated by the verse of fighting. It was also said: the meaning is that they have taken their religion, which they hold, as amusement and play, as in their treatment of the cattle, with those ignorances and misguidances mentioned earlier. It was also said: what is meant by "religion" here is the festival, that is, they took their festival as amusement and play. The clause ﴿and the life of this world has deceived them﴾ is coordinated with "they have taken," meaning: it deceived them until they preferred it over the Hereafter, denied the resurrection, and said: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected﴾.

His saying: ﴿And warn by it, lest a soul be delivered to destruction for what it has earned﴾. The pronoun in "bihi" (by it) refers to the Qur'an or to the reckoning.

Ibsāl means a person surrendering himself to destruction. From it comes "absaltu waladī," meaning I pledged my son in blood, because its outcome is destruction.

Al-Nābigha said:

*We pledged Āmir as a pledge for the Afāqa, for what was a pledge at al-Dardāʾ, so he was delivered up.*

That is, he perished. Al-Dardāʾ is a battalion that was well known among them by this name. So the meaning: warn by it, lest or for fear or dread that a soul perish for what it has earned, that is, be pledged and delivered to ruin. The original sense of ibsāl is restraint, and from it comes "shujāʿ bāsil," meaning a brave man who holds back from his opponent.

His saying: ﴿And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it﴾. Here "ʿadl" means ransom.

The meaning: even if that soul which has been delivered to destruction offers every ransom, that ransom will not be accepted from it, so that by it it might be saved from destruction. The subject of "yuʾkhadh" (be accepted) is a pronoun referring to ʿadl, since it carries the sense of the thing given as ransom, as in His saying: ﴿nor will any ransom be accepted from it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:48]. It was also said: its subject is "minhā" (from it), because here ʿadl is a verbal noun that cannot take a verb as its subject. "Kulla ʿadl" is in the accusative as a verbal noun: that is, ransom of every kind.

The demonstrative in His saying ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who took their religion as amusement and play, and its predicate is ﴿those who have been delivered to destruction for what they have earned﴾: that is, these people who took their religion as amusement and play are those who were delivered to destruction for what they earned. And ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾ is an answer to an assumed question, as if it were said: what is the condition of these people? So it is said: ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾, which is hot water. A similar expression is His saying: ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads﴾ [Al-Ḥajj 22:19]. Here it is a drink they drink, which cuts their intestines to pieces.

His saying: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides God, what neither benefits us nor harms us?﴾ God, glorified is He, commanded him to tell them this statement. The interrogative is for rebuke: that is, how can we call upon idols besides God, which do not benefit us in any way of benefit, if we want benefit from them, and which we do not fear the harm of in any way? Whoever is like this does not deserve worship. ﴿And be turned back on our heels﴾ is coordinated with "we call upon."

"Aʿqāb" is the plural of ʿaqib: that is, how can we call upon one who is like that and return to the misguidance from which God has brought us out?

Abū ʿUbayda said: it is said of one who is turned back from his need and does not obtain it, "he was turned back on his heels."

Al-Mubarrad said: we are repaid with evil after good. Its origin is from successive following (muʿāqaba) and "ʿuqbā," which are what follows something and must come after it. From it comes ﴿And the final outcome is for the God-fearing﴾ [Al-Qaṣaṣ 28:83]. From it comes ʿaqib (heel) of a man, and from it ʿuqūba (punishment), because it follows the sin.

His saying: ﴿Like one whom the devils have enticed on the earth﴾. Hawā (to fall) means to hasten toward something.

Al-Zajjāj said: it is from the desire of the soul, that is, Satan adorned his desire for him, and ﴿the devils have enticed him﴾ means they carried him off. The kāf in "ka-lladhī" is either an adjective to a deleted verbal noun, meaning: we are turned back upon our heels in a turning like that of one who..., or in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the subject of "nuraddu": that is, we are turned back (p-428) in a state of resembling him whom the devils have enticed, that is, the rebellious jinn have carried him off after he had been among mankind.

The majority read "istahawathu" (with the feminine pronoun). Ḥamza read "istahwāhu" in the masculine form, agreeing with the masculine collective noun.

Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan read "istahwāhu al-shayṭān" (the devil enticed him), and it is the same in the reading of Ubayy. "Ḥayrān" is a circumstantial state: that is, while he is bewildered and lost, not knowing how to act. Ḥayrān is one who does not find his way to any direction. One says "ḥāra ḥayratan wa-ḥayrūratan" when he wanders about. From this the stagnant water that has no outlet is named "ḥāʾir."

His saying: ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance﴾: this is a description of ḥayrān or a circumstantial clause: that is, he has companions who call him to guidance, saying to him, "Come to us," but he does not answer them and does not follow their guidance.

His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of God is the guidance﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to tell them: ﴿Indeed, the guidance of God﴾, that is, His religion which He has chosen for His servants, ﴿is the guidance﴾, and whatever is other than it is falsehood. ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:85]. "And we are commanded" is coordinated with the nominal sentence: that is, among what God commanded him to say. The lām in "li-nuslima" is the lām of cause, and what is caused is the command: that is, we were commanded for the purpose that we submit to the Lord of the worlds.

Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is we were commanded to submit, because the Arabs say "amartuka li-tadhhaba" (I commanded you so that you go) and "bi-an tadhhaba" with the same meaning.

Al-Naḥḥās said: I heard Ibn Kaysān say: it is the lām of the genitive (lām al-khafḍ).

His saying: ﴿And that you establish prayer and fear Him﴾ is coordinated with "li-nuslima," in the sense of "we were commanded to submit and to establish prayer." It may also be coordinated with "yadʿūnahu" in meaning: that is, they call him to guidance and call him to establish prayer.

﴿And He is the One to whom you will be gathered﴾, so how do you oppose His command?

﴿And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾: creating them with truth, or while the creation is in truth. So how do you worship idols, which are themselves created?

He said: ﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is, [His word is the truth]﴾. ﴿His word is the truth﴾ means: remember the day when He says, "Be," and it is; or, fear the day when He says, "Be," and it is. It was also said that it is a conjunction (ʿatf) with the pronoun in *wa-ittaquhu* (﴿and fear Him﴾). It was also said that *yawma* (the day) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf) governed by the sense of the clause ﴿His word is the truth﴾, and the meaning is: His command, which relates to things. *Al-Ḥaqq* (the truth) means: the one for whom it is witnessed that it is true. It was also said that *qawluhu* (His word) is the subject (mubtadaʾ), *al-ḥaqq* is its qualifier (ṣifah), and ﴿and the day He says, "Be," and it is﴾ is its predicate (khabar), placed before it. The meaning is: His word, qualified by truth, exists on the day when He says, "Be," and it is. It was also said that *qawluhu* is raised by *yakūnu* (it is), and *al-ḥaqq* is its qualifier, that is: on the day He says "Be," His word, the truth, will be.

Ibn ʿĀmir read *fa-nakūnu* with the nūn (we), and this indicates the speed of the reckoning. The rest read it with the yāʾ (he), which is the correct reading.

He said: ﴿And His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown﴾. The adverbial (ẓarf) is in the accusative, governed by what precedes it, that is: His is the dominion on this day. It was also said that it is a substitution (badal) for the first *yawm* (day). *Al-Ṣūr* (the Trumpet) is a horn into which the first blast is blown for annihilation and the second for re-creation. Al-Jawharī likewise said that *al-ṣūr* is the horn. The rajaz poet said:

*"We struck them on the morning of the two hosts, a violent strike, not like the strike of the two horns."*

*Al-Ṣūr* is pronounced with a ḍammah or a kasrah on the ṣād, as dialectal forms. It is reported from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd that he read *yawma yunfakhu fī al-ṣuwar* with the wāw vowelled, as the plural of *ṣūrah* (form), and the intended meaning is creation. Abū ʿUbaydah said: this, although possible, is rejected by what is in the Book and the Sunnah. Al-Farrāʾ said: *kun fa-yakūn* is said to refer to the Trumpet specifically, that is: and on the day He says to the Trumpet, "Be," and it is.

He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾. *ʿĀlimu* is raised because it is a qualifier of *alladhī khalaqa al-samāwāti wa-al-arḍ* (He who created the heavens and the earth). It is also permissible that it be raised by supposing an implied subject: that is, He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. It is reported from some of them that he read *yanfukhu* with the active form, and on this reading the subject may be ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾. It is also permissible that it be raised by an implied verb, as Sībawayh cited:

*"At your call, Yazid, a suppliant for a dispute, and one who is struck by what the calamities cast down."*

That is: *yubkīhi mukhtabiṭun* (one who is struck weeps for him).

Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read *ʿālimi* in the genitive, as a substitution (badal) for the pronoun in *lahu al-mulk* (His is the dominion). ﴿And He is the Wise﴾ in all that proceeds from Him, ﴿the Aware of everything﴾.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddī, regarding His saying ﴿And your people denied it﴾: he said, Quraysh denied the Qur'an. ﴿And it is the truth﴾. As for *al-wakīl* (the guardian), it means the one who preserves. As for ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾, the news of the people became fixed on the day of Badr by what He had promised them of punishment.

An-Naḥḥās narrated in his work on abrogation (naskh) from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾: he said, this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword (*āyat al-sayf*): ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5].

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: he said, it means a reality (ḥaqīqah).

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: its punishment is withheld until its sin is committed, then its punishment is released.

Ibn Jarīr narrated through al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: he said, it is an action and a reality, both what occurred of it in this world and what occurred of it in the Hereafter.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them﴾ and similar in the Qur'an: he said, Allah commanded the believers to unity, forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them that those before them were destroyed only through contention and disputes concerning the religion of Allah.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses﴾: he said, they mock them. He forbade Muḥammad (ﷺ) to sit with them, except if he forgets; when reminded, he should stand up. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿So do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn that he held that this verse was revealed concerning the people of desires (ahl al-ahwāʾ).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Abū Nuʿaym in *al-Ḥilyah* narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, who said: Do not sit with the people of disputes, for they are those who engage in vain talk concerning the verses of Allah.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, who said: the companions of desires are among those who engage in vain talk concerning the verses of Allah.

Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Muqātil, who said: when the polytheists in Mecca heard the Qur'an from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), they engaged in vain talk and mocked. The Muslims said: their company is not suitable for us, we fear that we would go out when we hear their words and sit with them, and then we would not blame them. So Allah revealed this verse.

Abū al-Shaykh also narrated from al-Suddī that he said: this verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

An-Naḥḥās narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿And upon those who fear Allah there is nothing of their reckoning﴾: he said, this Meccan verse was abrogated by the Medinan verse, which is His saying: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected and mocked, do not sit with them﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 140], and so on.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And upon those who fear Allah there is nothing of their reckoning﴾: if they sit, but they should not sit.

Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, that a group was brought to him who had sat drinking with a man who was fasting. He struck them and said: do not sit with them until they engage in talk other than that.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding His saying ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion﴾: he said, it is like His saying: ﴿Leave Me with whom I created alone﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11], meaning it is for threat (tahdīd).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Abū Dāwūd in his work on abrogation narrated from Qatādah regarding this verse: he said, it was abrogated by the verse of the sword.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from him regarding ﴿amusement and diversion﴾: he said, eating and drinking.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿lest a soul be delivered to ruin (an tubsala)﴾: he said, lest it be disgraced. And regarding ﴿they were delivered to ruin (ubsilū)﴾: he said, they were disgraced.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from him regarding ﴿They were delivered to ruin for what they earned﴾: he said, they were handed over for their misdeeds.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated from him regarding ﴿Say, "Shall we call upon other than Allah"﴾: he said, this is a parable that Allah struck for the idols and for the callers who call to other than Allah.

As for His saying ﴿like one whom the devils have lured in the earth﴾: it means they misled him. They are the ghouls (ghīlān) who call him by his name and his father's name and his grandfather's name, so he follows them and thinks he is in something, and in the morning they have cast him into destruction. Perhaps they eat him, or they cast him into a desert wasteland where he perishes of thirst. This is the likeness of one who answers the gods that are worshipped other than Allah.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated from him regarding ﴿like one whom the devils have lured﴾: he said, it is the man who does not respond to the guidance of Allah. He is the man who obeys the devil, acts in the earth with disobedience, deviates from the truth and strays from it. ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance﴾ and claim that what they command him is guidance. Allah says this about their allies among mankind: ﴿Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of Allah﴾, and misguidance is what the jinn call to.

Ibn al-Mubārak in *al-Zuhd*, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī (who graded it ḥasan), al-Nasāʾī, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Ḥākim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Baʿth* narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the Trumpet, and he said: it is a horn into which it is blown." The narrations concerning the manner of the blowing are established in the books of hadith, and we have no need to cite them here.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: he means that the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed is the One who blows into the Trumpet.

**Verse 68 onward**

His saying: ﴿But your people have denied it﴾. The pronoun refers either to the Qur'an or to the punishment.

"His people" who deny are the Quraysh. It was also said that they are every stubborn opponent. The clause ﴿while it is the truth﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl): that is, they denied the Qur'an or the punishment while it is true.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read "wa-kadhdhabat" with the feminine ta' (the verb agreeing with a feminine noun).

﴿Say: I am not a guardian over you﴾: that is, I am not a watcher over your deeds so that I would requite you for them.

It was said: this verse is abrogated (mansūkha) by the verse of fighting. It was also said: it is not abrogated, since their belief was not within his power.

His saying: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾: that is, for every matter there is a time in which it occurs.

Al-naba' is the thing about which news is given. It was also said that the meaning is: for every deed there is a recompense.

Al-Zajjāj said: it may be a threat to them with what will befall them in this world. Al-Ḥasan said: this is a threat from God to the disbelievers, because they did not acknowledge the resurrection. ﴿And you will soon know﴾ that it has come about and descended upon them, just as they knew on the day of Badr when what the Prophet (ﷺ) had threatened them with came to pass.

His saying: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them﴾. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), or to anyone suited to it.

Al-khawḍ (vain engagement) originally means wading in water. Then it was used for the depths of things that are unknown, by analogy with the depths of water, so it was borrowed from the sensible to the intelligible. It was also said that it is derived from mixing: everything you wade into you have mixed, and from it comes "khāḍa al-māʾ bi-l-ʿasal" (he mixed water with honey).

The meaning: when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, through denial, rejection and mockery, leave them and do not sit with them to hear such a grave wrong, until they engage in a discourse other than it. God, glorified is He, commanded him to turn away from the people of gatherings in which the signs of God are belittled, until they move on to discussing something else.

In this verse there is a great admonition for those who tolerate sitting with innovators (mubtadiʿa) who distort the speech of God, toy with His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and reduce these to their misguided desires and corrupt innovations. If one does not object to them or change what they are engaged in, then at the very least one should abandon sitting with them, and that is easy for him, not difficult.

They may make his presence with them, even while he is free from what they are involved in, a pretext by which they mislead the common people, so that his presence brings an additional harm beyond merely hearing the wrong.

We have witnessed from these cursed gatherings what cannot be counted. We have stood up in support of the truth and in repelling falsehood with what we were able to do and what our capacity reached. Whoever truly knows this purified Sharia will know that sitting with the people of misguided innovation carries a harm many times greater than sitting with one who disobeys God by committing some of the forbidden acts. This is especially so for one whose feet are not firmly planted in the knowledge of the Book and the Sunnah, for he may well be struck by their lies and nonsense, which are as manifestly false as can be. Then something will take root in his heart that is hard to cure and difficult to repel, so he acts upon it for the rest of his life and meets God with it, believing it to be the truth while it is among the most false of falsehoods and the most reprehensible of wrongs.

His saying: ﴿And if Satan causes you to forget, do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾. (Immā) here is the conditional particle, and it is usually followed by the emphatic nūn, though rarely not. From this is the poet's saying:

*If an enemy overtakes you in his own dwellings one day, then say: how can he rise and prevail?*

Ibn ʿAbbās read "yunassīka" with a doubled sīn. Similarly is the poet's saying:

*Indolence often makes you forget some of what you need.*

The meaning: if Satan has caused you to forget to rise and leave them, then ﴿do not sit after the reminder﴾, when you have remembered, ﴿with the wrongdoing people﴾, that is, those who wronged themselves by mocking the signs and denying them.

It was said: although the apparent address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), what is intended is an indirect warning to his community, because he is exempt from Satan causing him to forget. It was also said: there is no basis for this, since forgetting is permissible for him, as the authentic traditions have stated: "I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me," and similar.

His saying: ﴿Nor is there upon those who are God-fearing any account of them at all﴾: that is, upon those who fear God and avoid sitting with the disbelievers when they engage in vain talk concerning the signs of God, there is no reckoning for the disbelievers at all.

It was also said: the meaning is that upon those who fear God there is nothing for what occurs from them of vain talk concerning the signs of God during their sitting with them. According to this interpretation, the verse grants a concession to the God-fearing believers to sit with the disbelievers when they are compelled to do so, as will be mentioned when the occasion of revelation is recounted.

It was said: this concession was at the beginning of Islam, when the circumstances were those of taqiyya (dissimulation). Then God's saying was revealed: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the signs of God being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a discourse other than that﴾, and this abrogated that (naskh).

His saying: ﴿But it is a reminder, that perhaps they may fear God﴾. The word "dhikrā" (reminder) is in an accusative position as a verbal noun, or in a nominative position as a subject whose predicate is omitted: that is, "but upon them is a reminder."

Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "but this is a reminder."

The meaning, as an exception from the preceding negation, is: but upon them is the reminder to the disbelievers, through admonition and explanation to them that this is not permissible.

As for the first interpretation: merely avoiding the gatherings of those who engage in vain talk concerning the signs of God does not remove the obligation to command the right and forbid the wrong.

As for the second interpretation: the concession to sit does not remove the obligation of reminding, ﴿that perhaps they may fear God﴾ from vain talk concerning the signs of God, if the reminder from you reaches them.

As for making the pronoun refer to the God-fearing, this is very far-fetched.

His saying: ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and play﴾: that is, leave these people who have taken the religion, which they were obliged to act upon and enter into, as amusement and play. Do not hang your heart on them, for they are people of obstinacy, even though you are commanded to convey the proof to them.

It was said: this verse is abrogated by the verse of fighting. It was also said: the meaning is that they have taken their religion, which they hold, as amusement and play, as in their treatment of the cattle, with those ignorances and misguidances mentioned earlier. It was also said: what is meant by "religion" here is the festival, that is, they took their festival as amusement and play. The clause ﴿and the life of this world has deceived them﴾ is coordinated with "they have taken," meaning: it deceived them until they preferred it over the Hereafter, denied the resurrection, and said: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected﴾.

His saying: ﴿And warn by it, lest a soul be delivered to destruction for what it has earned﴾. The pronoun in "bihi" (by it) refers to the Qur'an or to the reckoning.

Ibsāl means a person surrendering himself to destruction. From it comes "absaltu waladī," meaning I pledged my son in blood, because its outcome is destruction.

Al-Nābigha said:

*We pledged Āmir as a pledge for the Afāqa, for what was a pledge at al-Dardāʾ, so he was delivered up.*

That is, he perished. Al-Dardāʾ is a battalion that was well known among them by this name. So the meaning: warn by it, lest or for fear or dread that a soul perish for what it has earned, that is, be pledged and delivered to ruin. The original sense of ibsāl is restraint, and from it comes "shujāʿ bāsil," meaning a brave man who holds back from his opponent.

His saying: ﴿And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it﴾. Here "ʿadl" means ransom.

The meaning: even if that soul which has been delivered to destruction offers every ransom, that ransom will not be accepted from it, so that by it it might be saved from destruction. The subject of "yuʾkhadh" (be accepted) is a pronoun referring to ʿadl, since it carries the sense of the thing given as ransom, as in His saying: ﴿nor will any ransom be accepted from it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:48]. It was also said: its subject is "minhā" (from it), because here ʿadl is a verbal noun that cannot take a verb as its subject. "Kulla ʿadl" is in the accusative as a verbal noun: that is, ransom of every kind.

The demonstrative in His saying ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who took their religion as amusement and play, and its predicate is ﴿those who have been delivered to destruction for what they have earned﴾: that is, these people who took their religion as amusement and play are those who were delivered to destruction for what they earned. And ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾ is an answer to an assumed question, as if it were said: what is the condition of these people? So it is said: ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾, which is hot water. A similar expression is His saying: ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads﴾ [Al-Ḥajj 22:19]. Here it is a drink they drink, which cuts their intestines to pieces.

His saying: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides God, what neither benefits us nor harms us?﴾ God, glorified is He, commanded him to tell them this statement. The interrogative is for rebuke: that is, how can we call upon idols besides God, which do not benefit us in any way of benefit, if we want benefit from them, and which we do not fear the harm of in any way? Whoever is like this does not deserve worship. ﴿And be turned back on our heels﴾ is coordinated with "we call upon."

"Aʿqāb" is the plural of ʿaqib: that is, how can we call upon one who is like that and return to the misguidance from which God has brought us out?

Abū ʿUbayda said: it is said of one who is turned back from his need and does not obtain it, "he was turned back on his heels."

Al-Mubarrad said: we are repaid with evil after good. Its origin is from successive following (muʿāqaba) and "ʿuqbā," which are what follows something and must come after it. From it comes ﴿And the final outcome is for the God-fearing﴾ [Al-Qaṣaṣ 28:83]. From it comes ʿaqib (heel) of a man, and from it ʿuqūba (punishment), because it follows the sin.

His saying: ﴿Like one whom the devils have enticed on the earth﴾. Hawā (to fall) means to hasten toward something.

Al-Zajjāj said: it is from the desire of the soul, that is, Satan adorned his desire for him, and ﴿the devils have enticed him﴾ means they carried him off. The kāf in "ka-lladhī" is either an adjective to a deleted verbal noun, meaning: we are turned back upon our heels in a turning like that of one who..., or in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the subject of "nuraddu": that is, we are turned back (p-428) in a state of resembling him whom the devils have enticed, that is, the rebellious jinn have carried him off after he had been among mankind.

The majority read "istahawathu" (with the feminine pronoun). Ḥamza read "istahwāhu" in the masculine form, agreeing with the masculine collective noun.

Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan read "istahwāhu al-shayṭān" (the devil enticed him), and it is the same in the reading of Ubayy. "Ḥayrān" is a circumstantial state: that is, while he is bewildered and lost, not knowing how to act. Ḥayrān is one who does not find his way to any direction. One says "ḥāra ḥayratan wa-ḥayrūratan" when he wanders about. From this the stagnant water that has no outlet is named "ḥāʾir."

His saying: ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance﴾: this is a description of ḥayrān or a circumstantial clause: that is, he has companions who call him to guidance, saying to him, "Come to us," but he does not answer them and does not follow their guidance.

His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of God is the guidance﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to tell them: ﴿Indeed, the guidance of God﴾, that is, His religion which He has chosen for His servants, ﴿is the guidance﴾, and whatever is other than it is falsehood. ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:85]. "And we are commanded" is coordinated with the nominal sentence: that is, among what God commanded him to say. The lām in "li-nuslima" is the lām of cause, and what is caused is the command: that is, we were commanded for the purpose that we submit to the Lord of the worlds.

Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is we were commanded to submit, because the Arabs say "amartuka li-tadhhaba" (I commanded you so that you go) and "bi-an tadhhaba" with the same meaning.

Al-Naḥḥās said: I heard Ibn Kaysān say: it is the lām of the genitive (lām al-khafḍ).

His saying: ﴿And that you establish prayer and fear Him﴾ is coordinated with "li-nuslima," in the sense of "we were commanded to submit and to establish prayer." It may also be coordinated with "yadʿūnahu" in meaning: that is, they call him to guidance and call him to establish prayer.

﴿And He is the One to whom you will be gathered﴾, so how do you oppose His command?

﴿And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾: creating them with truth, or while the creation is in truth. So how do you worship idols, which are themselves created?

He said: ﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is, [His word is the truth]﴾. ﴿His word is the truth﴾ means: remember the day when He says, "Be," and it is; or, fear the day when He says, "Be," and it is. It was also said that it is a conjunction (ʿatf) with the pronoun in *wa-ittaquhu* (﴿and fear Him﴾). It was also said that *yawma* (the day) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf) governed by the sense of the clause ﴿His word is the truth﴾, and the meaning is: His command, which relates to things. *Al-Ḥaqq* (the truth) means: the one for whom it is witnessed that it is true. It was also said that *qawluhu* (His word) is the subject (mubtadaʾ), *al-ḥaqq* is its qualifier (ṣifah), and ﴿and the day He says, "Be," and it is﴾ is its predicate (khabar), placed before it. The meaning is: His word, qualified by truth, exists on the day when He says, "Be," and it is. It was also said that *qawluhu* is raised by *yakūnu* (it is), and *al-ḥaqq* is its qualifier, that is: on the day He says "Be," His word, the truth, will be.

Ibn ʿĀmir read *fa-nakūnu* with the nūn (we), and this indicates the speed of the reckoning. The rest read it with the yāʾ (he), which is the correct reading.

He said: ﴿And His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown﴾. The adverbial (ẓarf) is in the accusative, governed by what precedes it, that is: His is the dominion on this day. It was also said that it is a substitution (badal) for the first *yawm* (day). *Al-Ṣūr* (the Trumpet) is a horn into which the first blast is blown for annihilation and the second for re-creation. Al-Jawharī likewise said that *al-ṣūr* is the horn. The rajaz poet said:

*"We struck them on the morning of the two hosts, a violent strike, not like the strike of the two horns."*

*Al-Ṣūr* is pronounced with a ḍammah or a kasrah on the ṣād, as dialectal forms. It is reported from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd that he read *yawma yunfakhu fī al-ṣuwar* with the wāw vowelled, as the plural of *ṣūrah* (form), and the intended meaning is creation. Abū ʿUbaydah said: this, although possible, is rejected by what is in the Book and the Sunnah. Al-Farrāʾ said: *kun fa-yakūn* is said to refer to the Trumpet specifically, that is: and on the day He says to the Trumpet, "Be," and it is.

He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾. *ʿĀlimu* is raised because it is a qualifier of *alladhī khalaqa al-samāwāti wa-al-arḍ* (He who created the heavens and the earth). It is also permissible that it be raised by supposing an implied subject: that is, He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. It is reported from some of them that he read *yanfukhu* with the active form, and on this reading the subject may be ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾. It is also permissible that it be raised by an implied verb, as Sībawayh cited:

*"At your call, Yazid, a suppliant for a dispute, and one who is struck by what the calamities cast down."*

That is: *yubkīhi mukhtabiṭun* (one who is struck weeps for him).

Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read *ʿālimi* in the genitive, as a substitution (badal) for the pronoun in *lahu al-mulk* (His is the dominion). ﴿And He is the Wise﴾ in all that proceeds from Him, ﴿the Aware of everything﴾.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddī, regarding His saying ﴿And your people denied it﴾: he said, Quraysh denied the Qur'an. ﴿And it is the truth﴾. As for *al-wakīl* (the guardian), it means the one who preserves. As for ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾, the news of the people became fixed on the day of Badr by what He had promised them of punishment.

An-Naḥḥās narrated in his work on abrogation (naskh) from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾: he said, this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword (*āyat al-sayf*): ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5].

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: he said, it means a reality (ḥaqīqah).

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: its punishment is withheld until its sin is committed, then its punishment is released.

Ibn Jarīr narrated through al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾: he said, it is an action and a reality, both what occurred of it in this world and what occurred of it in the Hereafter.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them﴾ and similar in the Qur'an: he said, Allah commanded the believers to unity, forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them that those before them were destroyed only through contention and disputes concerning the religion of Allah.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses﴾: he said, they mock them. He forbade Muḥammad (ﷺ) to sit with them, except if he forgets; when reminded, he should stand up. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿So do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn that he held that this verse was revealed concerning the people of desires (ahl al-ahwāʾ).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Abū Nuʿaym in *al-Ḥilyah* narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, who said: Do not sit with the people of disputes, for they are those who engage in vain talk concerning the verses of Allah.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, who said: the companions of desires are among those who engage in vain talk concerning the verses of Allah.

Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Muqātil, who said: when the polytheists in Mecca heard the Qur'an from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), they engaged in vain talk and mocked. The Muslims said: their company is not suitable for us, we fear that we would go out when we hear their words and sit with them, and then we would not blame them. So Allah revealed this verse.

Abū al-Shaykh also narrated from al-Suddī that he said: this verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

An-Naḥḥās narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿And upon those who fear Allah there is nothing of their reckoning﴾: he said, this Meccan verse was abrogated by the Medinan verse, which is His saying: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected and mocked, do not sit with them﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 140], and so on.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And upon those who fear Allah there is nothing of their reckoning﴾: if they sit, but they should not sit.

Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, that a group was brought to him who had sat drinking with a man who was fasting. He struck them and said: do not sit with them until they engage in talk other than that.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding His saying ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion﴾: he said, it is like His saying: ﴿Leave Me with whom I created alone﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11], meaning it is for threat (tahdīd).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Abū Dāwūd in his work on abrogation narrated from Qatādah regarding this verse: he said, it was abrogated by the verse of the sword.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from him regarding ﴿amusement and diversion﴾: he said, eating and drinking.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿lest a soul be delivered to ruin (an tubsala)﴾: he said, lest it be disgraced. And regarding ﴿they were delivered to ruin (ubsilū)﴾: he said, they were disgraced.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from him regarding ﴿They were delivered to ruin for what they earned﴾: he said, they were handed over for their misdeeds.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated from him regarding ﴿Say, "Shall we call upon other than Allah"﴾: he said, this is a parable that Allah struck for the idols and for the callers who call to other than Allah.

As for His saying ﴿like one whom the devils have lured in the earth﴾: it means they misled him. They are the ghouls (ghīlān) who call him by his name and his father's name and his grandfather's name, so he follows them and thinks he is in something, and in the morning they have cast him into destruction. Perhaps they eat him, or they cast him into a desert wasteland where he perishes of thirst. This is the likeness of one who answers the gods that are worshipped other than Allah.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated from him regarding ﴿like one whom the devils have lured﴾: he said, it is the man who does not respond to the guidance of Allah. He is the man who obeys the devil, acts in the earth with disobedience, deviates from the truth and strays from it. ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance﴾ and claim that what they command him is guidance. Allah says this about their allies among mankind: ﴿Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of Allah﴾, and misguidance is what the jinn call to.

Ibn al-Mubārak in *al-Zuhd*, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī (who graded it ḥasan), al-Nasāʾī, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Ḥākim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Baʿth* narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the Trumpet, and he said: it is a horn into which it is blown." The narrations concerning the manner of the blowing are established in the books of hadith, and we have no need to cite them here.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: he means that the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed is the One who blows into the Trumpet.

**Verse 68 onward**

His saying: ﴿But your people have denied it﴾. The pronoun refers either to the Qur'an or to the punishment.

"His people" who deny are the Quraysh. It was also said that they are every stubborn opponent. The clause ﴿while it is the truth﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl): that is, they denied the Qur'an or the punishment while it is true.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read "wa-kadhdhabat" with the feminine ta' (the verb agreeing with a feminine noun).

﴿Say: I am not a guardian over you﴾: that is, I am not a watcher over your deeds so that I would requite you for them.

It was said: this verse is abrogated (mansūkha) by the verse of fighting. It was also said: it is not abrogated, since their belief was not within his power.

His saying: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾: that is, for every matter there is a time in which it occurs.

Al-naba' is the thing about which news is given. It was also said that the meaning is: for every deed there is a recompense.

Al-Zajjāj said: it may be a threat to them with what will befall them in this world. Al-Ḥasan said: this is a threat from God to the disbelievers, because they did not acknowledge the resurrection. ﴿And you will soon know﴾ that it has come about and descended upon them, just as they knew on the day of Badr when what the Prophet (ﷺ) had threatened them with came to pass.

His saying: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them﴾. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), or to anyone suited to it.

Al-khawḍ (vain engagement) originally means wading in water. Then it was used for the depths of things that are unknown, by analogy with the depths of water, so it was borrowed from the sensible to the intelligible. It was also said that it is derived from mixing: everything you wade into you have mixed, and from it comes "khāḍa al-māʾ bi-l-ʿasal" (he mixed water with honey).

The meaning: when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, through denial, rejection and mockery, leave them and do not sit with them to hear such a grave wrong, until they engage in a discourse other than it. God, glorified is He, commanded him to turn away from the people of gatherings in which the signs of God are belittled, until they move on to discussing something else.

In this verse there is a great admonition for those who tolerate sitting with innovators (mubtadiʿa) who distort the speech of God, toy with His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and reduce these to their misguided desires and corrupt innovations. If one does not object to them or change what they are engaged in, then at the very least one should abandon sitting with them, and that is easy for him, not difficult.

They may make his presence with them, even while he is free from what they are involved in, a pretext by which they mislead the common people, so that his presence brings an additional harm beyond merely hearing the wrong.

We have witnessed from these cursed gatherings what cannot be counted. We have stood up in support of the truth and in repelling falsehood with what we were able to do and what our capacity reached. Whoever truly knows this purified Sharia will know that sitting with the people of misguided innovation carries a harm many times greater than sitting with one who disobeys God by committing some of the forbidden acts. This is especially so for one whose feet are not firmly planted in the knowledge of the Book and the Sunnah, for he may well be struck by their lies and nonsense, which are as manifestly false as can be. Then something will take root in his heart that is hard to cure and difficult to repel, so he acts upon it for the rest of his life and meets God with it, believing it to be the truth while it is among the most false of falsehoods and the most reprehensible of wrongs.

His saying: ﴿And if Satan causes you to forget, do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾. (Immā) here is the conditional particle, and it is usually followed by the emphatic nūn, though rarely not. From this is the poet's saying:

*If an enemy overtakes you in his own dwellings one day, then say: how can he rise and prevail?*

Ibn ʿAbbās read "yunassīka" with a doubled sīn. Similarly is the poet's saying:

*Indolence often makes you forget some of what you need.*

The meaning: if Satan has caused you to forget to rise and leave them, then ﴿do not sit after the reminder﴾, when you have remembered, ﴿with the wrongdoing people﴾, that is, those who wronged themselves by mocking the signs and denying them.

It was said: although the apparent address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), what is intended is an indirect warning to his community, because he is exempt from Satan causing him to forget. It was also said: there is no basis for this, since forgetting is permissible for him, as the authentic traditions have stated: "I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me," and similar.

His saying: ﴿Nor is there upon those who are God-fearing any account of them at all﴾: that is, upon those who fear God and avoid sitting with the disbelievers when they engage in vain talk concerning the signs of God, there is no reckoning for the disbelievers at all.

It was also said: the meaning is that upon those who fear God there is nothing for what occurs from them of vain talk concerning the signs of God during their sitting with them. According to this interpretation, the verse grants a concession to the God-fearing believers to sit with the disbelievers when they are compelled to do so, as will be mentioned when the occasion of revelation is recounted.

It was said: this concession was at the beginning of Islam, when the circumstances were those of taqiyya (dissimulation). Then God's saying was revealed: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the signs of God being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a discourse other than that﴾, and this abrogated that (naskh).

His saying: ﴿But it is a reminder, that perhaps they may fear God﴾. The word "dhikrā" (reminder) is in an accusative position as a verbal noun, or in a nominative position as a subject whose predicate is omitted: that is, "but upon them is a reminder."

Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "but this is a reminder."

The meaning, as an exception from the preceding negation, is: but upon them is the reminder to the disbelievers, through admonition and explanation to them that this is not permissible.

As for the first interpretation: merely avoiding the gatherings of those who engage in vain talk concerning the signs of God does not remove the obligation to command the right and forbid the wrong.

As for the second interpretation: the concession to sit does not remove the obligation of reminding, ﴿that perhaps they may fear God﴾ from vain talk concerning the signs of God, if the reminder from you reaches them.

As for making the pronoun refer to the God-fearing, this is very far-fetched.

His saying: ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and play﴾: that is, leave these people who have taken the religion, which they were obliged to act upon and enter into, as amusement and play. Do not hang your heart on them, for they are people of obstinacy, even though you are commanded to convey the proof to them.

It was said: this verse is abrogated by the verse of fighting. It was also said: the meaning is that they have taken their religion, which they hold, as amusement and play, as in their treatment of the cattle, with those ignorances and misguidances mentioned earlier. It was also said: what is meant by "religion" here is the festival, that is, they took their festival as amusement and play. The clause ﴿and the life of this world has deceived them﴾ is coordinated with "they have taken," meaning: it deceived them until they preferred it over the Hereafter, denied the resurrection, and said: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected﴾.

His saying: ﴿And warn by it, lest a soul be delivered to destruction for what it has earned﴾. The pronoun in "bihi" (by it) refers to the Qur'an or to the reckoning.

Ibsāl means a person surrendering himself to destruction. From it comes "absaltu waladī," meaning I pledged my son in blood, because its outcome is destruction.

Al-Nābigha said:

*We pledged Āmir as a pledge for the Afāqa, for what was a pledge at al-Dardāʾ, so he was delivered up.*

That is, he perished. Al-Dardāʾ is a battalion that was well known among them by this name. So the meaning: warn by it, lest or for fear or dread that a soul perish for what it has earned, that is, be pledged and delivered to ruin. The original sense of ibsāl is restraint, and from it comes "shujāʿ bāsil," meaning a brave man who holds back from his opponent.

His saying: ﴿And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it﴾. Here "ʿadl" means ransom.

The meaning: even if that soul which has been delivered to destruction offers every ransom, that ransom will not be accepted from it, so that by it it might be saved from destruction. The subject of "yuʾkhadh" (be accepted) is a pronoun referring to ʿadl, since it carries the sense of the thing given as ransom, as in His saying: ﴿nor will any ransom be accepted from it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:48]. It was also said: its subject is "minhā" (from it), because here ʿadl is a verbal noun that cannot take a verb as its subject. "Kulla ʿadl" is in the accusative as a verbal noun: that is, ransom of every kind.

The demonstrative in His saying ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who took their religion as amusement and play, and its predicate is ﴿those who have been delivered to destruction for what they have earned﴾: that is, these people who took their religion as amusement and play are those who were delivered to destruction for what they earned. And ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾ is an answer to an assumed question, as if it were said: what is the condition of these people? So it is said: ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾, which is hot water. A similar expression is His saying: ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads﴾ [Al-Ḥajj 22:19]. Here it is a drink they drink, which cuts their intestines to pieces.

His saying: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides God, what neither benefits us nor harms us?﴾ God, glorified is He, commanded him to tell them this statement. The interrogative is for rebuke: that is, how can we call upon idols besides God, which do not benefit us in any way of benefit, if we want benefit from them, and which we do not fear the harm of in any way? Whoever is like this does not deserve worship. ﴿And be turned back on our heels﴾ is coordinated with "we call upon."

"Aʿqāb" is the plural of ʿaqib: that is, how can we call upon one who is like that and return to the misguidance from which God has brought us out?

Abū ʿUbayda said: it is said of one who is turned back from his need and does not obtain it, "he was turned back on his heels."

Al-Mubarrad said: we are repaid with evil after good. Its origin is from successive following (muʿāqaba) and "ʿuqbā," which are what follows something and must come after it. From it comes ﴿And the final outcome is for the God-fearing﴾ [Al-Qaṣaṣ 28:83]. From it comes ʿaqib (heel) of a man, and from it ʿuqūba (punishment), because it follows the sin.

His saying: ﴿Like one whom the devils have enticed on the earth﴾. Hawā (to fall) means to hasten toward something.

Al-Zajjāj said: it is from the desire of the soul, that is, Satan adorned his desire for him, and ﴿the devils have enticed him﴾ means they carried him off. The kāf in "ka-lladhī" is either an adjective to a deleted verbal noun, meaning: we are turned back upon our heels in a turning like that of one who..., or in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the subject of "nuraddu": that is, we are turned back (p-428) in a state of resembling him whom the devils have enticed, that is, the rebellious jinn have carried him off after he had been among mankind.

The majority read "istahawathu" (with the feminine pronoun). Ḥamza read "istahwāhu" in the masculine form, agreeing with the masculine collective noun.

Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan read "istahwāhu al-shayṭān" (the devil enticed him), and it is the same in the reading of Ubayy. "Ḥayrān" is a circumstantial state: that is, while he is bewildered and lost, not knowing how to act. Ḥayrān is one who does not find his way to any direction. One says "ḥāra ḥayratan wa-ḥayrūratan" when he wanders about. From this the stagnant water that has no outlet is named "ḥāʾir."

His saying: ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance﴾: this is a description of ḥayrān or a circumstantial clause: that is, he has companions who call him to guidance, saying to him, "Come to us," but he does not answer them and does not follow their guidance.

His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of God is the guidance﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to tell them: ﴿Indeed, the guidance of God﴾, that is, His religion which He has chosen for His servants, ﴿is the guidance﴾, and whatever is other than it is falsehood. ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:85]. "And we are commanded" is coordinated with the nominal sentence: that is, among what God commanded him to say. The lām in "li-nuslima" is the lām of cause, and what is caused is the command: that is, we were commanded for the purpose that we submit to the Lord of the worlds.

Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is we were commanded to submit, because the Arabs say "amartuka li-tadhhaba" (I commanded you so that you go) and "bi-an tadhhaba" with the same meaning.

Al-Naḥḥās said: I heard Ibn Kaysān say: it is the lām of the genitive (lām al-khafḍ).

His saying: ﴿And that you establish prayer and fear Him﴾ is coordinated with "li-nuslima," in the sense of "we were commanded to submit and to establish prayer." It may also be coordinated with "yadʿūnahu" in meaning: that is, they call him to guidance and call him to establish prayer.

﴿And He is the One to whom you will be gathered﴾, so how do you oppose His command?
