Almighty God forbade eating what the name of God has not been mentioned over, after He had commanded eating what the name of God has been mentioned over.

In this is evidence for the prohibition of eating what the name of God has not been mentioned over.

The scholars (ahl al-'ilm) differed on this. Ibn 'Umar, his client Nafi', al-Sha'bi, and Ibn Sirin, and it is a narration from Malik and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu Thawr and Dawud al-Zahiri held this view: that what the name of God has not been mentioned over of slaughtered animals is forbidden, without distinction between one who does so deliberately and one who forgets, on the basis of this verse, and on the basis of His saying, exalted is He, in the verse on hunting: ﴿So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of God over it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 4]. What strengthens this inference further is His saying, exalted is He, in this verse: ﴿And indeed it is an abomination (fisq)﴾.

It has been established in sound hadiths that there is a command to mention the name of God (al-tasmiyah) in hunting and otherwise.

Al-Shafi'i and his companions, and it is a narration from Malik and a narration from Ahmad, held that mentioning the name (al-tasmiyah) is recommended (mustahabbah), not obligatory (wajibah). This is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah. Al-Shafi'i interpreted the verse as referring to one who slaughters for other than God, and this is a specification of the verse without a specifying evidence.

Abu Dawud related in the mursal narration that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The slaughter of a Muslim is lawful, whether the name of God was mentioned over it or not."

There is nothing in this mursal narration that is fit to specify the verse. Yes, the hadith of 'A'ishah, that she said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Some people bring us meat, and we do not know whether the name of God was mentioned over it or not?" He said: "Mention the name yourselves and eat," indicates that mentioning the name at the time of eating suffices when there is doubt about whether it was done at the time of slaughter.

Malik, Ahmad in the well-known view of him, Abu Hanifah and his companions, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh held that if the mentioning of the name is omitted through forgetfulness, it does no harm; but if it is omitted deliberately, the slaughtered animal is not lawful to eat.

This is narrated from 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata', Tawus, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu Malik, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman. They cited what al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If a Muslim forgets to mention the name when slaughtering, let him mention the name of God and let him eat it." This hadith, its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) is an error; it is in fact the statement of Ibn 'Abbas.

Likewise, 'Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir related it as his statement. Yes, it is possible to cite for this view something like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286], as its explanation has preceded, and His saying, peace and blessings of God be upon him: "Error and forgetfulness have been lifted from my community." As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which Ibn 'Adi related: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of God, what do you say about a man among us who slaughters and forgets to mention the name?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The name of God is upon every Muslim" — it is a weak hadith, which al-Bayhaqi and others have declared weak.

His saying: ﴿And indeed it is an abomination (fisq)﴾. The pronoun refers to "what" (ma), with an omitted modifier: i.e., and indeed eating what the name was not mentioned over is an abomination. It is also permissible for it to refer to the verbal noun of "you eat" (ta'kulu): i.e., indeed the eating is an abomination.

The meaning of fisq has already been verified.

Whoever took this verse to refer to what is slaughtered for other than God used His saying, "And indeed it is an abomination," and the basis of their inference is that omission is not fisq; rather, fisq is slaughtering for other than God.

This is answered by saying that applying the name fisq to one who abandons what God has obligated upon him is not legally impossible. ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾, i.e., they whisper to them with whisperings that oppose the truth and diverge from what is right, intending by that that these allies dispute with you using what they whisper to them. ﴿And if you obey them﴾ in what they command you and forbid you from, ﴿indeed you are then polytheists (mushrikun)﴾ like them.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The polytheists." In another wording: the Jews said: "Do not eat what God has killed, but eat what you yourselves have killed." So God revealed: ﴿And do not eat of what the name of God has not been mentioned over﴾.

Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh related from him, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿And do not eat of what the name of God has not been mentioned over﴾, Persia sent to Quraysh that they should dispute with Muhammad. They said to him: "What you slaughter with your hand with a knife is lawful, but what God slaughters with a golden shimshar, meaning carrion, is unlawful?!" Then this was revealed: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾. He said: "The devils are from Persia, and their allies are from Quraysh."

Something similar to what preceded has been narrated in the first hadith of Ibn 'Abbas through other chains.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh related from him also, regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾, he said: "Iblis inspired the polytheists of Quraysh."

Abu Dawud, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from him also, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not eat of what the name of God has not been mentioned over, and indeed it is an abomination﴾, that it was abrogated, and an exception was made from it, when He said: ﴿And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾.

'Abd ibn Humayd related from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Khatmi, who said: "Eat the slaughtered animals of the Muslims and the People of the Book, of what the name of God has been mentioned over."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Makhul something similar to the statement of Ibn 'Abbas regarding abrogation.

**His saying: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life﴾.**

The majority read the waw after the interrogative hamza with a fatha (فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ with the waw of the preceding word read as وَ with fatha).

Nafi' and Ibn Abi Nu'aym read it with sukun (saakin). Al-Nahhas said: It is permissible that it be understood according to the sense, meaning: "Look and reflect," ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than Allah?﴾, ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. What is meant by "the dead" here is the disbeliever whom Allah gave life through Islam. It was also said that the meaning is: he was dead when he was a drop of semen, and then We gave him life by breathing the spirit into him.

The first is preferable, because the context indicates it, since the verse is about warning the Muslims against following the polytheists. Life is often used figuratively for guidance and knowledge, and from this is the saying of the poet:

*Ignorance before death is a death for its people,*
*and their bodies before the graves are graves.*

*And a man who has not lived by knowledge is dead,*
*so for him there is no resurrection until the Resurrection.*

**Light** is an expression for guidance and faith. It was also said that it is the Qur'an, and it was said that it is wisdom, and it was said that it is the light mentioned in His saying: ﴿Their light runs before them and on their right hands﴾ [al-Hadid: 12]. The pronoun in *bihi* ("with it") refers back to the light.

﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾: that is, like one whose description is in darkness. *Mathaluhu* is the subject (mubtada') and *al-zulumat* is its predicate, and the clause is an attribute of *man*. It was also said that *mithl* ("like") is redundant, and the meaning is: "like one who is in darkness," as you say: "I am more honourable than the likes of you," meaning "than you." Similar to this is ﴿Then the recompense is like what he killed of the cattle﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95], and ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11].

It was also said that the meaning is: "like one whose likeness is the likeness of one who is in darkness," and ﴿not coming out of it﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal): that is, in a state of not coming out of it by any of the states.

**His saying (123): ﴿And thus We placed in every town great ones of its criminals to plot therein﴾**: that is, in the same manner of that placing, We placed in every town. *Al-akabir* is the plural of *akbar*. It was said: they are the leaders and the notables, and He singled them out for mention because they are more capable of corruption. *Al-makr* is the scheming in opposing uprightness, and its origin is twisting; the schemer twists away from uprightness, that is, turns away from it. ﴿And they plot only against themselves﴾: that is, the harm of their scheming returns upon them. ﴿And they do not perceive it﴾ because of the extreme of their ignorance.

**(124): ﴿And when a sign comes to them﴾** among the signs, ﴿they say: "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah."﴾ They mean that they will not believe until they themselves become prophets. This is a strange kind of their peculiar ignorance and their wondrous arrogance. A parallel to it is ﴿Every man among them wants to be given scrolls spread out﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 52].

The meaning: when a sign came to the great ones, they said this statement. So Allah answered them with His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾: that is, Allah knows best who deserves to be made a messenger and to be the place for it and its trustee. He has chosen to place the message in Muhammad, His chosen one and His beloved, so leave off seeking what is not of your concern. He threatened them with His saying: ﴿Humiliation will befall those who committed crime﴾: that is, abasement and disgrace. Its origin is from *sighar* (smallness), as if abasement makes a person reduce himself. It was also said that *sigar* is being content with abasement; this was narrated from Ibn al-Sikkit.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life﴾, that he said: he was a disbeliever, astray, and We guided him. ﴿And We made for him a light﴾ is the Qur'an. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾: of disbelief and misguidance.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah concerning the verse that he said: it was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, that it refers to Umar ibn al-Khattab, ﴿like one whose likeness is in darkness, not coming out of it﴾ refers to Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam concerning the verse that he said: it was revealed concerning Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. They were both dead in their misguidance, so Allah gave life to Umar through Islam and honoured him, and left Abu Jahl in his misguidance and his death. This was because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) supplicated, saying: "O Allah, strengthen Islam through Abu Jahl ibn Hisham or through Umar ibn al-Khattab."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿And thus We placed in every town great ones of its criminals﴾ that he said: it was revealed concerning the mockers.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning the verse, that he said: We empowered its wicked ones, so they disobeyed in it; and when they did that, We destroyed them with punishment.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid who said: ﴿great ones of its criminals﴾: its nobles.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Jurayj concerning His saying: ﴿And when a sign comes to them﴾, the verse. He said: They said to Muhammad when he invited them to what he invited them to of the truth: "If this were true, there would be among us someone more deserving to be given it than Muhammad." ﴿And they said: Why was this Qur'an not revealed upon a great man from the two towns?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31].

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Humiliation will befall those who committed crime﴾, that he said: "They associated partners with Allah." ﴿Humiliation﴾: he said: disgrace.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 6, verses 125–128:

His saying: ﴿Whoever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾. Al-sharh (expansion) is splitting, and its origin is widening. "Sharahtu al-amr" means I clarified and explained it. The meaning: whoever Allah wills to guide to the truth, He widens his breast until he accepts it with an expanded breast. ﴿And whoever He wills to misguide﴾ ﴿He makes his breast constricted and tight﴾.

Ibn Kathir read "ḍayqan" with light stress, like hayn and layn.

The rest read it with the doubled letter, and both are dialectal variants (lughatan).

Nafi' read "ḥarajan" with a kasra, and its meaning is constricted (al-ḍayyiq); he repeated the meaning for emphasis, and the variation in wording made it good.

The rest read it with a fatha, the plural of ḥarajah, which is intense constriction. Al-ḥarajah is also rage, and its plurals are ḥuraj and ḥurujat. From this comes the phrase "fulan yataharraj," meaning he constricts himself (yuḍayyiq ʿalā nafsihi).

Al-Jawhari said: "makanun ḥarijun wa ḥarajun" means a constricted place, thick with trees, which the grazing animal cannot reach. Al-ḥarij also means sin.

Al-Zajjaj said: al-ḥaraj is the extreme of constriction.

Al-Nahhas said: "ḥarij" is the active participle, while ḥaraj is a verbal noun used as an adjective, as one says "rajulun ʿadlun" (a just man).

His saying: ﴿as if he were climbing up into the sky﴾.

Ibn Kathir read it with light stress, from al-ṣuʿud (ascending), likening the disbeliever's burden of faith upon him to one who forces himself to do what he cannot bear, like climbing to the sky.

Al-Nakha'i read "yaṣṣāʿad," whose origin is yatasāʿad.

The rest read ﴿yaṣṣaʿʿad﴾ with the doubled letters, whose origin is yataṣaʿʿad, and its meaning is: he forces himself to do what he cannot bear again and again, as one who wishes to ascend to the sky forces himself.

It has been said that the meaning in all readings is: his heart nearly ascends to the sky out of aversion to Islam. The "mā" in "ka'annamā" is the particle (muhayyi'ah) that prepares "ka'anna" to enter upon verbal sentences.

His saying: ﴿Thus Allah places filth upon those who do not believe﴾. That is: like that placing, which is making the breast constricted and tight, Allah places the filth (al-rijs).

Al-rijs in language is stench. It has been said it is punishment, and it has been said it is Satan whom Allah sets upon them, and it has been said it is that which has no good in it. The first meaning is the well-known one in the language of the Arabs, and it is used figuratively for the punishment that befalls them, and it is true of all the meanings mentioned.

The reference in His saying: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord﴾ is to what the Prophet (ﷺ) and those believers with him follow; that is, this is the path of your Lord's religion, with no crookedness in it. It has been said the reference is to what was mentioned earlier that indicates success and abandonment, that is, this is Allah's custom with His servants: He guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills. The accusative of ﴿straight﴾ is in the status of a circumstantial state (ḥāl), like His saying: ﴿And it is the truth, confirming﴾ [al-Baqarah: 91] and ﴿This is my husband, an old man﴾ [Hud: 72].

﴿We have detailed the signs﴾, that is, we have explained and clarified them ﴿for a people who remember﴾, who reflect upon what is in them and understand their meanings.

The "bi" in ﴿for what they used to do﴾ is causal: that is, because of their deeds.

His saying: ﴿And on the day He gathers them all﴾. The time-expression is in the accusative governed by an implied verb placed before it: that is, remember the day He gathers them; or ﴿and on the day He gathers them﴾ we say: ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾. The intended meaning is the gathering of all creation on the Resurrection. Al-ma'shar means the group; that is, on the Day of Gathering we say: O group of jinn, ﴿you have taken much of mankind﴾, that is, in enjoying them, as in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others﴾ [al-An'am: 128]. It has also been said: you have taken much from their misguidance and their leading astray, until they came under your authority as followers, so We gather them with you. Similar is the saying: "al-amir istakthara min al-junud" (the commander took many soldiers). The intent is reproach and rebuke. According to the first view, enjoyment means the jinn's delight in mankind's obedience to them and their entry into what they desire from them. ﴿And their allies from mankind will say: Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others﴾.

As for the jinn's enjoyment of mankind, it is what preceded: their delight in following them. As for mankind's enjoyment of the jinn, it is that when they accepted from them the embellishment of sins, they fell into them and delighted in them; that is their enjoyment of the jinn. It has been said: mankind's enjoyment of the jinn is that when a man passed through a valley on his journey and feared for himself, he would say: "I seek refuge in the Lord of this valley from all that I fear," meaning their lord among the jinn. From this is His saying: ﴿And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in distress﴾ [al-Jinn: 6]. It has been said: the jinn's enjoyment of mankind is that they believed them in what they said of false unseen reports, and mankind's enjoyment of the jinn is that they delighted in what the jinn conveyed to them of falsehoods and obtained by that some share of worldly fortunes, like the soothsayers. ﴿And we have reached our term which You set for us﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, acknowledging their arrival at what Allah promised them, which they used to deny.

When they said this statement, Allah answered them, so ﴿He said: The Fire is your abode﴾, that is, the place of your stay.

Al-mathwa means the stay. The sentence is a resumed answer to an implied question.

His saying: ﴿Abiding therein, except what Allah wills﴾. The meaning required by the Arabic language in this construction is that they abide in the Fire at all times except the time when Allah wills their non-remaining in it.

Al-Zajjaj said: the exception refers to the Day of Resurrection, that is, abiding in the Fire except what Allah wills of the duration of their gathering from their graves and the length of their time in reckoning. This is a strained view, because the exception is from perpetual abiding, and it does not apply to one who has not entered the Fire. It has been said: the exception is for the people of faith, and "mā" is in the sense of "man": that is, except whomever Allah wills faith for, for he does not enter the Fire. It has been said: the meaning is: except what Allah wills of their being in the world without punishment.

All these interpretations are forced, and what compelled them to them is what came in the Quranic verses and the prophetic hadiths about the eternal abiding of the disbelievers in the Fire forever. But there is no contradiction between a general and a specific ruling, especially after its recurrence in the Qur'an, as will come in Surah Hud: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is the Doer of what He intends﴾ [Hud: 107]. Perhaps more verification will come there, if Allah wills.

They said: How does He expand his breast, O Messenger of Allah? He said: A light is cast into it, and his breast is expanded and widened for it. They said: Is there a sign by which one may recognize it? He said: Turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before the coming of death."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related similar from Fudayl. Ibn Abi al-Dunya related similar from al-Hasan as well.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab have related through various chains from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when this verse was revealed, said [something] similar, and he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh related it from him, as a marfu' report, through another chain.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat, and Ibn al-Najjar in his history have related from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mustawrid, who was a descendant of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, and he mentioned something similar.

These chains strengthen one another, and a connected chain strengthens a mursal one, so the adoption of this prophetic explanation is necessary.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse, he said: Just as the son of Adam cannot reach the sky, so he cannot have faith and monotheism enter his heart until Allah causes it to enter his heart.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Jabir ibn Zayd, who said: al-Salam is Allah.

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, who said: Allah is al-Salam, and His abode is Paradise.

Ibn Mardawayh related it from him, as a marfu' report, through another chain.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat, and Ibn al-Najjar in his history have related from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mustawrid, who was a descendant of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, and he mentioned something similar.

These chains strengthen one another, and a connected chain strengthens a mursal one, so the adoption of this prophetic explanation is necessary.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse, he said: Just as the son of Adam cannot reach the sky, so he cannot have faith and monotheism enter his heart until Allah causes it to enter his heart.

al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat related from him regarding the verse, he says: Whoever Allah wills to misguide, He constricts upon him until He makes Islam tight for him, while Islam is wide. This is when He says: ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78], meaning: He has not placed upon you any constriction in Islam.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿abode of peace﴾, he said: Paradise.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Jabir ibn Zayd, who said: al-Salam is Allah.

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, who said: Allah is al-Salam, and His abode is Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿you have taken much of mankind﴾, he says: from your misguidance of them, meaning you led many of them astray. And regarding His saying: ﴿abiding therein except what Allah wills﴾, he said: this verse does not befit anyone to judge concerning Allah in His creation, that He does not cause them to enter Paradise or Fire.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 6, verses 125–128:

His saying: ﴿Whoever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾. Al-sharh (expansion) is splitting, and its origin is widening. "Sharahtu al-amr" means I clarified and explained it. The meaning: whoever Allah wills to guide to the truth, He widens his breast until he accepts it with an expanded breast. ﴿And whoever He wills to misguide﴾ ﴿He makes his breast constricted and tight﴾.

Ibn Kathir read "ḍayqan" with light stress, like hayn and layn.

The rest read it with the doubled letter, and both are dialectal variants (lughatan).

Nafi' read "ḥarajan" with a kasra, and its meaning is constricted (al-ḍayyiq); he repeated the meaning for emphasis, and the variation in wording made it good.

The rest read it with a fatha, the plural of ḥarajah, which is intense constriction. Al-ḥarajah is also rage, and its plurals are ḥuraj and ḥurujat. From this comes the phrase "fulan yataharraj," meaning he constricts himself (yuḍayyiq ʿalā nafsihi).

Al-Jawhari said: "makanun ḥarijun wa ḥarajun" means a constricted place, thick with trees, which the grazing animal cannot reach. Al-ḥarij also means sin.

Al-Zajjaj said: al-ḥaraj is the extreme of constriction.

Al-Nahhas said: "ḥarij" is the active participle, while ḥaraj is a verbal noun used as an adjective, as one says "rajulun ʿadlun" (a just man).

His saying: ﴿as if he were climbing up into the sky﴾.

Ibn Kathir read it with light stress, from al-ṣuʿud (ascending), likening the disbeliever's burden of faith upon him to one who forces himself to do what he cannot bear, like climbing to the sky.

Al-Nakha'i read "yaṣṣāʿad," whose origin is yatasāʿad.

The rest read ﴿yaṣṣaʿʿad﴾ with the doubled letters, whose origin is yataṣaʿʿad, and its meaning is: he forces himself to do what he cannot bear again and again, as one who wishes to ascend to the sky forces himself.

It has been said that the meaning in all readings is: his heart nearly ascends to the sky out of aversion to Islam. The "mā" in "ka'annamā" is the particle (muhayyi'ah) that prepares "ka'anna" to enter upon verbal sentences.

His saying: ﴿Thus Allah places filth upon those who do not believe﴾. That is: like that placing, which is making the breast constricted and tight, Allah places the filth (al-rijs).

Al-rijs in language is stench. It has been said it is punishment, and it has been said it is Satan whom Allah sets upon them, and it has been said it is that which has no good in it. The first meaning is the well-known one in the language of the Arabs, and it is used figuratively for the punishment that befalls them, and it is true of all the meanings mentioned.

The reference in His saying: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord﴾ is to what the Prophet (ﷺ) and those believers with him follow; that is, this is the path of your Lord's religion, with no crookedness in it. It has been said the reference is to what was mentioned earlier that indicates success and abandonment, that is, this is Allah's custom with His servants: He guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills. The accusative of ﴿straight﴾ is in the status of a circumstantial state (ḥāl), like His saying: ﴿And it is the truth, confirming﴾ [al-Baqarah: 91] and ﴿This is my husband, an old man﴾ [Hud: 72].

﴿We have detailed the signs﴾, that is, we have explained and clarified them ﴿for a people who remember﴾, who reflect upon what is in them and understand their meanings.

﴿For them is the abode of peace with their Lord﴾, that is, for these who remember, is Paradise, because it is the abode of safety from every hated thing; or it is the abode of the Lord, the Peace, stored up for them with their Lord, who will bring them to it. ﴿And He is their Protector﴾, that is, their helper. The "bi" in ﴿for what they used to do﴾ is causal: that is, because of their deeds.

His saying: ﴿And on the day He gathers them all﴾. The time-expression is in the accusative governed by an implied verb placed before it: that is, remember the day He gathers them; or ﴿and on the day He gathers them﴾ we say: ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾. The intended meaning is the gathering of all creation on the Resurrection. Al-ma'shar means the group; that is, on the Day of Gathering we say: O group of jinn, ﴿you have taken much of mankind﴾, that is, in enjoying them, as in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others﴾ [al-An'am: 128]. It has also been said: you have taken much from their misguidance and their leading astray, until they came under your authority as followers, so We gather them with you. Similar is the saying: "al-amir istakthara min al-junud" (the commander took many soldiers). The intent is reproach and rebuke. According to the first view, enjoyment means the jinn's delight in mankind's obedience to them and their entry into what they desire from them. ﴿And their allies from mankind will say: Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others﴾.

As for the jinn's enjoyment of mankind, it is what preceded: their delight in following them. As for mankind's enjoyment of the jinn, it is that when they accepted from them the embellishment of sins, they fell into them and delighted in them; that is their enjoyment of the jinn. It has been said: mankind's enjoyment of the jinn is that when a man passed through a valley on his journey and feared for himself, he would say: "I seek refuge in the Lord of this valley from all that I fear," meaning their lord among the jinn. From this is His saying: ﴿And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in distress﴾ [al-Jinn: 6]. It has been said: the jinn's enjoyment of mankind is that they believed them in what they said of false unseen reports, and mankind's enjoyment of the jinn is that they delighted in what the jinn conveyed to them of falsehoods and obtained by that some share of worldly fortunes, like the soothsayers. ﴿And we have reached our term which You set for us﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, acknowledging their arrival at what Allah promised them, which they used to deny.

When they said this statement, Allah answered them, so ﴿He said: The Fire is your abode﴾, that is, the place of your stay.

Al-mathwa means the stay. The sentence is a resumed answer to an implied question.

His saying: ﴿Abiding therein, except what Allah wills﴾. The meaning required by the Arabic language in this construction is that they abide in the Fire at all times except the time when Allah wills their non-remaining in it.

Al-Zajjaj said: the exception refers to the Day of Resurrection, that is, abiding in the Fire except what Allah wills of the duration of their gathering from their graves and the length of their time in reckoning. This is a strained view, because the exception is from perpetual abiding, and it does not apply to one who has not entered the Fire. It has been said: the exception refers to the Fire: that is, except what Allah wills of their punishment by other than it at some times, such as the zamharir (extreme cold). It has been said: the exception is for the people of faith, and "mā" is in the sense of "man": that is, except whomever Allah wills faith for, for he does not enter the Fire. It has been said: the meaning is: except what Allah wills of their being in the world without punishment.

All these interpretations are forced, and what compelled them to them is what came in the Quranic verses and the prophetic hadiths about the eternal abiding of the disbelievers in the Fire forever. But there is no contradiction between a general and a specific ruling, especially after its recurrence in the Qur'an, as will come in Surah Hud: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is the Doer of what He intends﴾ [Hud: 107]. Perhaps more verification will come there, if Allah wills.

Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat have related from Abu Ja'far al-Madai'ni, a man from Banu Hashim, and he is not Muhammad ibn 'Ali, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about this verse: ﴿Whoever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾. They said: How does He expand his breast, O Messenger of Allah? He said: A light is cast into it, and his breast is expanded and widened for it. They said: Is there a sign by which one may recognize it? He said: Turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before the coming of death."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related similar from Fudayl. Ibn Abi al-Dunya related similar from al-Hasan as well.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab have related through various chains from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when this verse was revealed, said [something] similar, and he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh related it from him, as a marfu' report, through another chain.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat, and Ibn al-Najjar in his history have related from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mustawrid, who was a descendant of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, and he mentioned something similar.

These chains strengthen one another, and a connected chain strengthens a mursal one, so the adoption of this prophetic explanation is necessary.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse, he said: Just as the son of Adam cannot reach the sky, so he cannot have faith and monotheism enter his heart until Allah causes it to enter his heart.

al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat related from him regarding the verse, he says: Whoever Allah wills to misguide, He constricts upon him until He makes Islam tight for him, while Islam is wide. This is when He says: ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78], meaning: He has not placed upon you any constriction in Islam.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿abode of peace﴾, he said: Paradise.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Jabir ibn Zayd, who said: al-Salam is Allah.

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi, who said: Allah is al-Salam, and His abode is Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿you have taken much of mankind﴾, he says: from your misguidance of them, meaning you led many of them astray. And regarding His saying: ﴿abiding therein except what Allah wills﴾, he said: this verse does not befit anyone to judge concerning Allah in His creation, that He does not cause them to enter Paradise or Fire.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 6, verses 129–132:

His words: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, meaning: just as We placed between the jinn and mankind what has preceded. ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾. The meaning is: We make some of them take others as allies (tawallaa), so they become allies of one another, and then some of them disavow others. So the meaning of "nuwallee" (We make [them] allies) on this reading is: We make him an ally (waliyy) of him.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: its meaning is that We give power to the oppressors among the jinn over the oppressors among mankind.

It is also narrated from him that he explained this verse as meaning: We give power to some of the oppressors over others, so that he destroys them and humiliates them. Thus, on this reading, the verse contains a threat to the oppressors: whoever among them does not refrain from oppressing [others], God will set over him another oppressor.

Fudayl ibn ʿIyad said: When you see an oppressor taking revenge on an oppressor, stand back and look on in wonder. It was also said: the meaning of "nuwallee" is: We leave some of them to others in what they choose of disbelief. The "bi" in ﴿for what they used to earn﴾ is causal (sababiyya): that is, because of their earning of sins, We made some of them allies of others.

His words: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ That is, on the day We gather them, We will say to them: ﴿Did there not come to you...﴾; or it is the beginning of a report of what will happen at the gathering. Its apparent meaning is that God sends messengers to the jinn in this world from among them, just as He sends messengers to mankind from among them. It was also said: the meaning of "from among you" is: from among those who are of your kind in creation, obligation, and the intended addressee, for the jinn and mankind share in that. Even if the messengers were only from mankind, they are of the same kind as the jinn in that respect. It was also said: this is by way of giving precedence to mankind over the jinn, as the male is given precedence over the female. It was also said: what is meant by the messengers to the jinn here is the warners (nudhur) from among them, as in His words: ﴿They returned to their people as warners﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29].

His words: ﴿who recount to you My verses﴾ are another attribute of the messengers; the explanation of the meaning of "qass" (recounting) has already been given.

His words: ﴿They will say: We bear witness against ourselves﴾. This is an acknowledgment from them that God's proof is binding upon them through the sending of His messengers to them. The clause is a response to an implied question, so it is independent (mustaʾnafa). The clause ﴿and the life of this world deceived them﴾ is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), or it is a parenthetical clause (muʿtaridha). ﴿And they bore witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers﴾: this is another testimony from them against themselves that they were disbelievers in the world, in regard to the messengers sent to them and the signs they brought. What has preceded indicates that verses like this one, which explicitly state their admission of disbelief against themselves, and like their saying: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], are to be understood as meaning that they admit in some stations of the Day of Resurrection and deny in others, because of the length of that day, the agitation of hearts in it, the confusion of minds, the closing of understandings and the dulling of intellects.

The indication in His words "that" (dhalika) refers either to their testimony against themselves or to the sending of the messengers to them.

The "an" in ﴿that your Lord would not destroy the cities﴾ is the light (mukhaffafa) form of the heavy (thaqila), and its subject is a omitted pronoun of the matter (damir shaʾn).

The meaning: "That is because the matter is: your Lord would not destroy the cities..." Or it is the verbal (masdariyya) "an", and the "bi" in "bi-zulm" is causal: that is, I would not have destroyed the cities because of the wrongdoing of those among them who do wrong, while their people are heedless, and God had not sent to them a messenger.

The meaning: God sent the messengers to His servants, because He does not destroy from the cities whoever disobeys Him with disbelief, while they are heedless of the admonition and warning through the sending of messengers and the revelation of books. Rather, He destroys them only after the sending of messengers to them and the lifting of heedlessness from them through the warning of the prophets to them: ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15]. It was also said: the meaning is: God would not destroy the people of the cities through injustice from Him, for He, glory be to Him, is exalted above injustice; rather He destroys them only after they deserve it and heedlessness is lifted from them through the sending of the prophets. It was also said: the meaning is: God does not destroy the people of the cities because of the wrongdoing of those among them who do wrong, while the others are heedless of that; this is like His words: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164].

﴿And for all there are degrees according to what they did﴾: that is, for each of the jinn and mankind there are varying degrees according to what they did, and We will repay them for their deeds, as He said in another verse: ﴿And for all there are degrees according to what they did, and that He may fully repay them their deeds, and they will not be wronged﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 19]. In it is evidence that the obedient among the jinn are in Paradise and the disobedient are in the Fire. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾ of deeds of good and evil. Heedlessness (ghaflah) is the departure of a thing from you because you are occupied with something else.

Ibn ʿAmir read "taʿmalun" with the second-person (taʾ), while the rest read it with the third-person (yaʾ). (p-449)

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, that he said: God makes some of the wrongdoers allies of others in this world, and they follow one another into the Fire.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd regarding the verse the same as what we related from him above.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Aʿmash regarding the explanation of the verse, he said: I heard them saying: When the time becomes corrupt, the worst of them are placed in authority over them.

Al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab narrated through the chain of Yahya ibn Hashim: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "As you are, so you will be ruled over."

Al-Bayhaqi said: This is disconnected (munqatiʿ), and Yahya is weak.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿messengers from among you﴾, he said: There are no messengers among the jinn; rather the messengers are among mankind, and warning is among the jinn, and he recited: ﴿And when it was decreed, they returned to their people as warners﴾.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh, in al-ʿAzama as well, narrated from al-Dahhak, who said: The jinn enter Paradise and eat and drink.

Abu al-Shaykh, in al-ʿAzama as well, narrated from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who said: The Muslim jinn enter neither Paradise nor the Fire, because God expelled their father from Paradise, so He will not return him nor his offspring.

Abu al-Shaykh, in al-ʿAzama as well, narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Creation is of four kinds: a kind all of whom are in Paradise, a kind all of whom are in the Fire, and two kinds who are in both Paradise and the Fire. As for those who are all in Paradise, they are the angels; as for those who are all in the Fire, they are the devils; and as for those in both Paradise and the Fire, they are mankind and the jinn, for them is reward and upon them is punishment.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 6, verses 129–132:

His words: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, meaning: just as We placed between the jinn and mankind what has preceded. ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾. The meaning is: We make some of them take others as allies (tawallaa), so they become allies of one another, and then some of them disavow others. So the meaning of "nuwallee" (We make [them] allies) on this reading is: We make him an ally (waliyy) of him.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: its meaning is that We give power to the oppressors among the jinn over the oppressors among mankind.

It is also narrated from him that he explained this verse as meaning: We give power to some of the oppressors over others, so that he destroys them and humiliates them. Thus, on this reading, the verse contains a threat to the oppressors: whoever among them does not refrain from oppressing [others], God will set over him another oppressor.

Fudayl ibn ʿIyad said: When you see an oppressor taking revenge on an oppressor, stand back and look on in wonder. It was also said: the meaning of "nuwallee" is: We leave some of them to others in what they choose of disbelief. The "bi" in ﴿for what they used to earn﴾ is causal (sababiyya): that is, because of their earning of sins, We made some of them allies of others.

His words: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ That is, on the day We gather them, We will say to them: ﴿Did there not come to you...﴾; or it is the beginning of a report of what will happen at the gathering. Its apparent meaning is that God sends messengers to the jinn in this world from among them, just as He sends messengers to mankind from among them. It was also said: the meaning of "from among you" is: from among those who are of your kind in creation, obligation, and the intended addressee, for the jinn and mankind share in that. Even if the messengers were only from mankind, they are of the same kind as the jinn in that respect. It was also said: this is by way of giving precedence to mankind over the jinn, as the male is given precedence over the female. It was also said: what is meant by the messengers to the jinn here is the warners (nudhur) from among them, as in His words: ﴿They returned to their people as warners﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29].

His words: ﴿who recount to you My verses﴾ are another attribute of the messengers; the explanation of the meaning of "qass" (recounting) has already been given.

His words: ﴿They will say: We bear witness against ourselves﴾. This is an acknowledgment from them that God's proof is binding upon them through the sending of His messengers to them. The clause is a response to an implied question, so it is independent (mustaʾnafa). The clause ﴿and the life of this world deceived them﴾ is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), or it is a parenthetical clause (muʿtaridha). ﴿And they bore witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers﴾: this is another testimony from them against themselves that they were disbelievers in the world, in regard to the messengers sent to them and the signs they brought. What has preceded indicates that verses like this one, which explicitly state their admission of disbelief against themselves, and like their saying: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], are to be understood as meaning that they admit in some stations of the Day of Resurrection and deny in others, because of the length of that day, the agitation of hearts in it, the confusion of minds, the closing of understandings and the dulling of intellects.

The indication in His words "that" (dhalika) refers either to their testimony against themselves or to the sending of the messengers to them.

The "an" in ﴿that your Lord would not destroy the cities﴾ is the light (mukhaffafa) form of the heavy (thaqila), and its subject is a omitted pronoun of the matter (damir shaʾn).

The meaning: "That is because the matter is: your Lord would not destroy the cities..." Or it is the verbal (masdariyya) "an", and the "bi" in "bi-zulm" is causal: that is, I would not have destroyed the cities because of the wrongdoing of those among them who do wrong, while their people are heedless, and God had not sent to them a messenger.

The meaning: God sent the messengers to His servants, because He does not destroy from the cities whoever disobeys Him with disbelief, while they are heedless of the admonition and warning through the sending of messengers and the revelation of books. Rather, He destroys them only after the sending of messengers to them and the lifting of heedlessness from them through the warning of the prophets to them: ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15]. It was also said: the meaning is: God would not destroy the people of the cities through injustice from Him, for He, glory be to Him, is exalted above injustice; rather He destroys them only after they deserve it and heedlessness is lifted from them through the sending of the prophets. It was also said: the meaning is: God does not destroy the people of the cities because of the wrongdoing of those among them who do wrong, while the others are heedless of that; this is like His words: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164].

﴿And for all there are degrees according to what they did﴾: that is, for each of the jinn and mankind there are varying degrees according to what they did, and We will repay them for their deeds, as He said in another verse: ﴿And for all there are degrees according to what they did, and that He may fully repay them their deeds, and they will not be wronged﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 19]. In it is evidence that the obedient among the jinn are in Paradise and the disobedient are in the Fire. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾ of deeds of good and evil. Heedlessness (ghaflah) is the departure of a thing from you because you are occupied with something else.

Ibn ʿAmir read "taʿmalun" with the second-person (taʾ), while the rest read it with the third-person (yaʾ). (p-449)

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, that he said: God makes some of the wrongdoers allies of others in this world, and they follow one another into the Fire.

As for those who are all in Paradise, they are the angels; as for those who are all in the Fire, they are the devils; and as for those in both Paradise and the Fire, they are mankind and the jinn, for them is reward and upon them is punishment.

The Lord is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani) ﴿Your Lord is the Self-Sufficient﴾, meaning He is independent of His creation: He has no need of them or of their worship. Their faith does not benefit Him, and their disbelief does not harm Him. Yet, although He is free of need for them, He is Merciful toward them. His independence from them does not prevent His mercy toward them. How excellent this divine statement is, and how eloquent. How strong is the linking of independence and mercy in this context, for mercy toward them together with independence from them is the utmost of bounty and grace. ﴿If He wills, He can remove you﴾, O servants who disobey, and uproot you with a punishment that leads to destruction, and ﴿replace after you whomever He wills of His creation﴾, of those who are more obedient to Him and quicker to comply with His rulings than you. ﴿As He produced you from the offspring of another people﴾. The kāf (ka) is an adjective (na't) for a deleted infinitive (maṣdar), and mā is a maṣdariyyah (verbal-noun particle). The meaning is: He will replace you with a replacement like the production of you from the offspring of another people. It was said that they were the people of Noah's ship. But He, glorified is He, did not will that, so He did not destroy them nor replace them with others, out of mercy toward them and kindness to them.

134. ﴿What you are promised﴾ of resurrection and recompense ﴿is surely coming, and you cannot escape﴾, because God does not break His promise. ﴿And you cannot escape﴾ means you cannot get away from what is descending upon you and befalling you. It is said: "So-and-so outpaced me" (a'jazanī fulān), meaning he got away from me and overcame me.

Allah's statement: ﴿Say: O my people, act according to your standing﴾. The makānah means the way or manner. The meaning is: remain upon what you are upon, for I am indifferent to you and unconcerned with your disbelief. I am steadfast upon what I am upon. ﴿You will surely come to know﴾ who is upon the truth and who is upon falsehood. This is a severe warning. Therefore, the question of how He commands them to persist in disbelief does not arise. ﴿The ultimate outcome of the abode﴾ is the praiseworthy outcome by which its possessor is praised, meaning: whoever has victory in the abode of this world, whoever has inheritance of the earth, and whoever has the Abode of the Hereafter.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of makānatikum is your establishment (tamakkunukum) in this world. That is, act upon your firm position regarding your affair. It was also said: upon your side, and it was said: upon your place.

Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read "man yakūnu" with the yā' (third person), while the rest read it with the tā' (second person).

The pronoun in ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers do not prosper﴾ refers to the matter (li-al-sha'n): that is, one who is characterized by the attribute of wrongdoing does not prosper. This is an indirect rebuke to them, that they will not prosper because they are characterized by wrongdoing.

Allah's statement: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has produced of crops and livestock﴾. This is an explanation of another type of their disbelief, ignorance, and their giving precedence to their gods over Allah, glorified is He. That is: they assigned to Allah, glorified is He, a share of what He created from their crops and the offspring of their animals, and to their gods a share of that, which they spend on their attendants and those who serve them. When what was for their gods is consumed by spending on it, they compensated from what they had assigned to Allah, and said: "Allah is independent of that." Al-za'm means falsehood.

Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb, al-Sulamī, al-A'mash and al-Kisā'ī read bi-za'mihim with a ḍammah on the zāy, while the rest read it with a fatḥah. Both are dialectal variants. ﴿So what was for their partners does not reach Allah﴾, meaning it does not reach the channels which Allah legislated for spending, such as charity, maintaining family ties, and hospitality to guests. ﴿And what was for Allah reaches their partners﴾, meaning they make it for their gods and spend it on their interests. ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, meaning evil is their judgment in preferring their gods over Allah, glorified is He. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: when they slaughtered what they had assigned to Allah, they mentioned upon it the name of their idols, and when they slaughtered what was for their idols, they did not mention upon it the name of Allah. This is the meaning of "reaching Allah" and "reaching their partners." We have already discussed the word dhara'a.

Allah's statement: ﴿And likewise, their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾. That is: and similar to that adornment which Satan adorned for them in dividing their wealth between Allah and their partners, he adorned for them the killing of their children.

Al-Farrā' and al-Zajjāj said: "their partners" here are those who used to serve the idols. It was said: they are the misguided among people. It was said: they are the devils. He indicated by this the wa'd, which is burying daughters out of fear of captivity and poverty. It was also said: a man would swear by Allah that if he had such-and-such number of sons, he would slaughter one of them, as 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib did.

The majority read zayyana with the active voice, with qatla in the accusative as the object of zayyana, and awlādi in the genitive by the qatla being in construct with it, and shurakā'uhum in the nominative as the subject of zayyana. Al-Ḥasan read it with a ḍammah on the zāy, raising qatla, lowering awlād, and raising shurakā'uhum, so that qatla is the deputy subject (nā'ib al-fā'il). Shurakā'uhum is raised by the estimated verb yajʿalu returning to it, meaning: "their partners adorned it." A similar example is the poet's words:

"Let Yazīd weep, the one who is humbled by a dispute, and the one who is bewildered by what the calamities strike."

That is, the one humbled weeps for him.

Ibn 'Āmir and the people of Syria read with a ḍammah on the zāy, raising qatla, accusing awlād, and lowering shurakā'ihim, so that qatla is in construct with shurakā'ihim, and its object is awlāduhum. In this there is a separation between the verbal noun and what is in construct with it by the object. A similar example of separating the verbal noun from its genitive is the poet's words:

"She passes over what she persists in, and the nobles of 'Abd al-Qays have wiped clean their breasts from them."

The genitive of ṣudūrihā is used, and the estimate is: the nobles of 'Abd al-Qays have wiped clean from them the breasts of her ṣudūr.

Al-Naḥḥās said: this reading is not permissible in speech or in poetry. The grammarians only permitted separating between the construct and the genitive with an adverb in poetry, because of their latitude with adverbs. Separating with the object in poetry is remote, so permitting it in the Qur'an is even more remote.

Abū Ghānim Aḥmad ibn Ḥimdān, the grammarian, said: this reading of Ibn 'Āmir is not permissible in Arabic, and it is a slip of a scholar. When a scholar slips, it is not permissible to follow him, and his statement is returned to the consensus. They only permitted, out of necessity for the poet, separating between the construct and the genitive by an adverb, as in the poet's words:

"As the scribe wrote the book with the hand of a Jew, one day, approaching or removing."

And the other's words:

"By Allah, what a plight today for the one who blamed her."

Some who defended this reading said: if it is established by mass transmission (tawātur) from the Prophet (ﷺ), then it is eloquent and not ugly.

They said: this has occurred in the speech of the Arabs, and in the Muṣḥaf of 'Uthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, the word "shurakā'ihim" is written with a yā'.

I say: the claim of mass transmission is false, by the consensus of the reliable readers, as we have explained in a separate treatise. Whoever reads in a way that contradicts the grammatical aspect, his reading is rejected. It is not valid to argue for the soundness of this reading by what has occurred of separation in verse, as we have already mentioned, and like the poet's words:

"So I shoved her with a shove, the shove of the camel-colt by my father Mazādah."

The necessity of poetry is not measured by it. In the verse there is a fourth reading, which is the genitive of awlād and shurakā'. The explanation for that is that shurakā' is an appositive (badal) for awlād, because they are their partners in lineage and inheritance.

Allah's statement: ﴿So that they might destroy them﴾. The lām is the lām of purpose (lām kay), meaning: in order that they may destroy them, from al-irdā', which is destruction. ﴿And that they might confuse for them their religion﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it, meaning: they did that adornment to destroy them and to mix their religion for them. ﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have done it﴾, meaning: if Allah had willed that they not do it, they would not have done it. What He wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur. And since that is by Allah's will, ﴿leave them and what they fabricate﴾, so leave them and their fabrication, for that will not harm you.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Abān ibn 'Uthmān, who said: al-dhurriyyah is the origin, and al-dhurriyyah is the offspring.

They also both narrated from Ibn 'Abbās regarding ﴿and you cannot escape﴾, that he said: "outpacing."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from him regarding Allah's statement ﴿upon your standing﴾, that he said: upon your side.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan also narrated from him regarding Allah's statement ﴿And they assigned to Allah﴾ the verse, that he said: They assigned to Allah a share of their fruits and their water, and a share to Satan and the idols. If what they assigned to Allah fell into the share of Satan, they left it. If what they assigned to the devils fell into the share of Allah, they returned it to the share of Satan. If water flowing from irrigating what they assigned to Allah went into the share of Satan, they left it. If water flowing from irrigating what they assigned to Satan went into the share of Allah, they drained it. This is what they assigned to Allah from the crops and the irrigation water. As for what they assigned to Satan from the livestock, it is Allah's statement: ﴿Allah did not appoint any bahīrah﴾ (Al-Mā'idah 5:103), the verse.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from him something similar by another route.

It was also said: a man would swear by Allah that if he had such-and-such number of sons, he would slaughter one of them, as 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib did.

The majority read zayyana with the active voice, with qatla in the accusative as the object of zayyana, and awlādi in the genitive by the qatla being in construct with it, and shurakā'uhum in the nominative as the subject of zayyana. Al-Ḥasan read it with a ḍammah on the zāy, raising qatla, lowering awlād, and raising shurakā'uhum, so that qatla is the deputy subject (nā'ib al-fā'il). Shurakā'uhum is raised by the estimated verb yajʿalu returning to it, meaning: "their partners adorned it." A similar example is the poet's words:

"Let Yazīd weep, the one who is humbled by a dispute, and the one who is bewildered by what the calamities strike."

That is, the one humbled weeps for him.

Ibn 'Āmir and the people of Syria read with a ḍammah on the zāy, raising qatla, accusing awlād, and lowering shurakā'ihim, so that qatla is in construct with shurakā'ihim, and its object is awlāduhum. In this there is a separation between the verbal noun and what is in construct with it by the object. A similar example of separating the verbal noun from its genitive is the poet's words:

"She passes over what she persists in, and the nobles of 'Abd al-Qays have wiped clean their breasts from them."

The genitive of ṣudūrihā is used, and the estimate is: the nobles of 'Abd al-Qays have wiped clean from them the breasts of her ṣudūr.

Al-Naḥḥās said: this reading is not permissible in speech or in poetry. The grammarians only permitted separating between the construct and the genitive with an adverb in poetry, because of their latitude with adverbs. Separating with the object in poetry is remote, so permitting it in the Qur'an is even more remote.

Abū Ghānim Aḥmad ibn Ḥimdān, the grammarian, said: this reading of Ibn 'Āmir is not permissible in Arabic, and it is a slip of a scholar. When a scholar slips, it is not permissible to follow him, and his statement is returned to the consensus. They only permitted, out of necessity for the poet, separating between the construct and the genitive by an adverb, as in the poet's words:

"As the scribe wrote the book with the hand of a Jew, one day, approaching or removing."

And the other's words:

"By Allah, what a plight today for the one who blamed her."

Some who defended this reading said: if it is established by mass transmission (tawātur) from the Prophet (ﷺ), then it is eloquent and not ugly.

They said: this has occurred in the speech of the Arabs, and in the Muṣḥaf of 'Uthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, the word "shurakā'ihim" is written with a yā'.

I say: the claim of mass transmission is false, by the consensus of the reliable readers, as we have explained in a separate treatise. Whoever reads in a way that contradicts the grammatical aspect, his reading is rejected. It is not valid to argue for the soundness of this reading by what has occurred of separation in verse, as we have already mentioned, and like the poet's words:

"So I shoved her with a shove, the shove of the camel-colt by my father Mazādah."

The necessity of poetry is not measured by it. In the verse there is a fourth reading, which is the genitive of awlād and shurakā'. The explanation for that is that shurakā' is an appositive (badal) for awlād, because they are their partners in lineage and inheritance.

Allah's statement: ﴿So that they might destroy them﴾. The lām is the lām of purpose (lām kay), meaning: in order that they may destroy them, from al-irdā', which is destruction. ﴿And that they might confuse for them their religion﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it, meaning: they did that adornment to destroy them and to mix their religion for them. ﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have done it﴾, meaning: if Allah had willed that they not do it, they would not have done it. What He wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur. And since that is by Allah's will, ﴿leave them and what they fabricate﴾, so leave them and their fabrication, for that will not harm you.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Abān ibn 'Uthmān, who said: al-dhurriyyah is the origin, and al-dhurriyyah is the offspring.

They also both narrated from Ibn 'Abbās regarding ﴿and you cannot escape﴾, that he said: "outpacing."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from him regarding Allah's statement ﴿upon your standing﴾, that he said: upon your side.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan also narrated from him regarding Allah's statement ﴿And they assigned to Allah﴾ the verse, that he said: They assigned to Allah a share of their fruits and their water, and a share to Satan and the idols. If what they assigned to Allah fell into the share of Satan, they left it. If what they assigned to the devils fell into the share of Allah, they returned it to the share of Satan. If water flowing from irrigating what they assigned to Allah went into the share of Satan, they left it. If water flowing from irrigating what they assigned to Satan went into the share of Allah, they drained it. This is what they assigned to Allah from the crops and the irrigation water. As for what they assigned to Satan from the livestock, it is Allah's statement: ﴿Allah did not appoint any bahīrah﴾ (Al-Mā'idah 5:103), the verse.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from him something similar by another route.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid, who said: They assigned to Allah a portion of what He produced of crops, and a portion to their partners. Whatever the wind carried from what they had named for Allah into the portion of their idols, they left it and said, "Allah is independent of this." And whatever the wind carried from the portion of their idols into the portion of Allah, they took it.

The livestock they named for Allah were the baḥīrah and the sā'ibah.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Mujāhid regarding Allah's statement ﴿And likewise, their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾ that he said: Their devils commanded them to bury their children out of fear of poverty.

The Lord is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani) ﴿Your Lord is the Self-Sufficient﴾, meaning He is independent of His creation: He has no need of them or of their worship. Their faith does not benefit Him, and their disbelief does not harm Him. Yet, although He is free of need for them, He is Merciful toward them. His independence from them does not prevent His mercy toward them. How excellent this divine statement is, and how eloquent. How strong is the linking of independence and mercy in this context, for mercy toward them together with independence from them is the utmost of bounty and grace. ﴿If He wills, He can remove you﴾, O servants who disobey, and uproot you with a punishment that leads to destruction, and ﴿replace after you whomever He wills of His creation﴾, of those who are more obedient to Him and quicker to comply with His rulings than you. ﴿As He produced you from the offspring of another people﴾. The kāf (ka) is an adjective (na't) for a deleted infinitive (maṣdar), and mā is a maṣdariyyah (verbal-noun particle). The meaning is: He will replace you with a replacement like the production of you from the offspring of another people. It was said that they were the people of Noah's ship. But He, glorified is He, did not will that, so He did not destroy them nor replace them with others, out of mercy toward them and kindness to them.

134. ﴿What you are promised﴾ of resurrection and recompense ﴿is surely coming, and you cannot escape﴾, because God does not break His promise. ﴿And you cannot escape﴾ means you cannot get away from what is descending upon you and befalling you. It is said: "So-and-so outpaced me" (a'jazanī fulān), meaning he got away from me and overcame me.

Allah's statement: ﴿Say: O my people, act according to your standing﴾. The makānah means the way or manner. The meaning is: remain upon what you are upon, for I am indifferent to you and unconcerned with your disbelief. I am steadfast upon what I am upon. ﴿You will surely come to know﴾ who is upon the truth and who is upon falsehood. This is a severe warning. Therefore, the question of how He commands them to persist in disbelief does not arise. ﴿The ultimate outcome of the abode﴾ is the praiseworthy outcome by which its possessor is praised, meaning: whoever has victory in the abode of this world, whoever has inheritance of the earth, and whoever has the Abode of the Hereafter.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of makānatikum is your establishment (tamakkunukum) in this world. That is, act upon your firm position regarding your affair. It was also said: upon your side, and it was said: upon your place.

Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read "man yakūnu" with the yā' (third person), while the rest read it with the tā' (second person).

The pronoun in ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers do not prosper﴾ refers to the matter (li-al-sha'n): that is, one who is characterized by the attribute of wrongdoing does not prosper. This is an indirect rebuke to them, that they will not prosper because they are characterized by wrongdoing.

Allah's statement: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has produced of crops and livestock﴾. This is an explanation of another type of their disbelief, ignorance, and their giving precedence to their gods over Allah, glorified is He. That is: they assigned to Allah, glorified is He, a share of what He created from their crops and the offspring of their animals, and to their gods a share of that, which they spend on their attendants and those who serve them. When what was for their gods is consumed by spending on it, they compensated from what they had assigned to Allah, and said: "Allah is independent of that." Al-za'm means falsehood.

Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb, al-Sulamī, al-A'mash and al-Kisā'ī read bi-za'mihim with a ḍammah on the zāy, while the rest read it with a fatḥah. Both are dialectal variants. ﴿So what was for their partners does not reach Allah﴾, meaning it does not reach the channels which Allah legislated for spending, such as charity, maintaining family ties, and hospitality to guests. ﴿And what was for Allah reaches their partners﴾, meaning they make it for their gods and spend it on their interests. ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, meaning evil is their judgment in preferring their gods over Allah, glorified is He. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: when they slaughtered what they had assigned to Allah, they mentioned upon it the name of their idols, and when they slaughtered what was for their idols, they did not mention upon it the name of Allah. This is the meaning of "reaching Allah" and "reaching their partners." We have already discussed the word dhara'a.

Allah's statement: ﴿And likewise, their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾. That is: and similar to that adornment which Satan adorned for them in dividing their wealth between Allah and their partners, he adorned for them the killing of their children.
